messages.body_plain:
That sounds great. I put an example on github at: https://github.com/mostly-harmless/select2shiny

Tool4 in ui.R does almost what I would like. When you hit 'destroy' the selection box offers the opportunity to use the shift-key to select many options. But ... what I would like it to (1) search for all options that end, for example, in '-a' and then use the shift key to select all of them. Fine-tuning with the select and destroy buttons is nice as is. Any ideas?

For others that might want to see what select2 looks like:
shiny::runGitHub('select2shiny','mostly-harmless')

messages.subject: Re: UI: positioning widgets (UI elements) side by side.
messages.subject_clean: UI: positioning widgets (UI elements) side by side.
messages.body_plain:
You can do this:

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  # ... any elements you want here ...
))

This will give you a completely empty page to put whatever inputs, outputs, or HTML you want, but with the necessary JS and CSS for Bootstrap preloaded and ready to use. Here's a simple bootstrap example:

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  div(class="container",
    div(class="row",
      div(class="span4", "hi"),
      div(class="span4",
        selectInput("foo", "Foo", 1:8),
        selectInput("bar", "Bar", 9:16)
      )
    )
    tags$hr()
    tags$style(type="text/css",
      " /* some CSS rules */ ",
      " /* some more rules */ "
    )
  )
))

if (!require(quantmod)) {
  stop("This app requires the quantmod package. To install it, run 'install.packages(\"quantmod\")'.\n")

}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Make a chart for a symbol, with the settings from the inputs
  make_chart <- function(symbol) {

    ###############################################################################
    # Load Systematic Investor Toolbox (SIT)
    # http://systematicinvestor.wordpress.com/systematic-investor-toolbox/
    ###############################################################################
    setInternet2(TRUE)
    con = gzcon(url('http://www.systematicportfolio.com/sit.gz', 'rb'))
    source(con)
    close(con)
    load.packages('quantmod')

    # download sample data from Yahoo

    data.spy = getSymbols('symbol', from = '2010-01-01', auto.assign = FALSE)

                          y = data.spy['2011:01:01::2011:02:01']
                          highlight = which(Cl(y) < 127)

                          png(filename = 'plot1.png', width = 500, height = 500, units = 'px', pointsize = 12, bg = 'white')

                          layout(c(1,1,2))
                          plota(y, type = 'candle', main = 'SPY', plotX = F, x.highlight = highlight)
                          y = plota.scale.volume(y)
                          plota(y, type = 'volume', x.highlight = highlight)

                          dev.off()

  }

  output$plot_aapl <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("AAPL") })
  output$plot_msft <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("MSFT") })
  output$plot_ibm <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("IBM") })
  output$plot_goog <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("GOOG") })
  output$plot_yhoo <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("YHOO") })
})

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  sidebarPanel(

      checkboxInput(inputId = "stock_yhoo", label = "Yahoo (YHOO)", value = FALSE)
    )),

  mainPanel(
    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_aapl",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_aapl"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_msft",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_msft"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_ibm",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_ibm"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_goog",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_goog"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_yhoo",

))

messages.body_plain:
Joe and Vincent,

Thank you guys so much for your work on getting "select2" functioning within the Shiny framework. I have been trying to figure out how to get something like this working now for over a week and I just don't have enough Javascript skills to do so. I was also attempting to get jQuery-Multiselect working within a "reactiveUI" context, but have been falling short. I realize now it comes down to the following code chunk:

> $(document).ready(function() { $("#packData").select2({ width: 'resolve', placeholder: "Choose a file" }); });

and I just don't know how to compensate for it.
I would much rather utilize "select2" than "jQuery-MultiSelect" since it has the same look and feel of "native" shiny UI objects. I am glad someone else has an interest in extending the selectInput functionality beyond the basic.

Joe ... there have been a lot of good "output" extension examples in this group, such as FooTable and DataTable, but not a really solid "input" extension example. I went through the "building-input" tutorial along with Kenton Russell's d3 example in this group which extends outputs according to what is laid out on the Shiny website. However, trying to tackle the addition of some of the necessary Shiny functions within the default select2.js file is a daunting task for a javascript newbie. I think if you could provide a solid example of how to transform "select2" to a functioning Shiny component, this will open the door for so many other people to follow that example and extend other existing Javascript UI components.

Thanks so much for all you are doing with Shiny! Your work and effort is greatly appreciated.

messages.subject: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
I'm interested in using Shiny in a situation where proxies don't support web sockets.

Is there a fundamental reason that Shiny couldn't just use AJAX rather than web sockets?  I took a look through the code and it looks like it is using raw web sockets on the client side (new WebSocket(...)).

On the server side is it using SockJS?  I thought the point of SockJS is that it could fall back on a non-websocket transport in situations where it wasn't available.  And it has a client library to make this possible in a cross-browser way?  But I guess the R side only support web sockets.

I'd be interested to hear any thoughts on this, and also any pointers if there is documentation about the client/server protocol.  Thanks!

Andy

Hello Joe Cheng [RStudio]

I  created ui.R and server.R based on the example given in stocks  http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/

####### server.R########

if (!require(quantmod)) {
  stop("This app requires the quantmod package. To install it, run 'install.packages(\"quantmod\")'.\n")
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Make a chart for a symbol, with the settings from the inputs
  make_chart <- function(symbol) {

    ###############################################################################
    # Load Systematic Investor Toolbox (SIT)
    # http://systematicinvestor.wordpress.com/systematic-investor-toolbox/
    ###############################################################################
    setInternet2(TRUE)
    con = gzcon(url('http://www.systematicportfolio.com/sit.gz', 'rb'))
    source(con)
    close(con)
    load.packages('quantmod')

    # download sample data from Yahoo
    data.spy = getSymbols('symbol', from = '2010-01-01', auto.assign = FALSE)

                          y = data.spy['2011:01:01::2011:02:01']
                          highlight = which(Cl(y) < 127)

                          png(filename = 'plot1.png', width = 500, height = 500, units = 'px', pointsize = 12, bg = 'white')

                          layout(c(1,1,2))
                          plota(y, type = 'candle', main = 'SPY', plotX = F, x.highlight = highlight)
                          y = plota.scale.volume(y)
                          plota(y, type = 'volume', x.highlight = highlight)

                          dev.off()

  }

  output$plot_aapl <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("AAPL") })
  output$plot_msft <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("MSFT") })
  output$plot_ibm <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("IBM") })
  output$plot_goog <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("GOOG") })
  output$plot_yhoo <- reactivePlot(function() { make_chart("YHOO") })
})

  mainPanel(
    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_aapl",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_aapl"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_msft",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_msft"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_ibm",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_ibm"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_goog",
                     br(),
                     div(plotOutput(outputId = "plot_goog"))),

    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.stock_yhoo",
                     br(),
                     plotOutput(outputId = "plot_yhoo"))
  )
))

messages.subject: Re: Tutorial - Problems building Application
messages.body_plain:
The problem is with this part:
  url('http://www.systematicportfolio.com/sit.gz', 'rb')

That URL gets a 302 redirect to another URL. It appears that on Mac and Linux, the url() function apparently gives an error when it encounters a redirect, but on Windows, it will successfully follow a redirect.

I would suggest downloading the sit.gz file yourself, unzipping it, and saving in the same directory as your Shiny app. Then you can source the file in your app. This will avoid the error, and it will also be more efficient - there's no need to download the file each time your app is used.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Store results of different users?
messages.body_plain:
You can store a separate R object for every visitor, by declaring that object within

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  # here!
})

The server function is executed once at the beginning of each page load, so any local variables in that scope belong to you alone.

If you want your outputs to change when the R object changes, then you want to use reactiveValues:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  userValues <- reactiveValues()
  userValues$clicks <- c()

  observe(function() {
    # make_dataframe_from_input is just a stand-in for however you turn your jquery
    # input into the dataframe or whatever that you need
    userValues$clicks <- make_dataframe_from_input(input$clicks)
  })

  output$table <- reactiveTable({
    userValues$clicks
  })
})

To actually collect the mouse clicks you'll need to write an input binding, there's a tutorial section <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#building-inputs> for that.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
If you use Shiny Server (and you should!), you should be able to proxy it through non-websocket-supporting proxies. We use SockJS on the Shiny Server side, then Shiny Server opens a websocket connection to the backend R process (localhost-to-localhost).

On Sat, Feb 2, 2013 at 12:12 PM, Andy Chu <andy...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I'm interested in using Shiny in a situation where proxies don't support web sockets.
>
> Is there a fundamental reason that Shiny couldn't just use AJAX rather than web sockets?  I took a look through the code and it looks like it is using raw web sockets on the client side (new WebSocket(...)).
>
> On the server side is it using SockJS?  I thought the point of SockJS is that it could fall back on a non-websocket transport in situations where it wasn't available.  And it has a client library to make this possible in a cross-browser way?  But I guess the R side only support web sockets.
>
> I'd be interested to hear any thoughts on this, and also any pointers if there is documentation about the client/server protocol.  Thanks!

>
>
> Andy
>

messages.subject: Re: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
messages.subject_clean: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
messages.body_plain:
Sorry Alex, didn't mean to ignore this one. I was pretty sure this was going to be a problem but I didn't have a great solution. I don't love the idea of *everything* being an array all the time, but at the same time it is pretty surprising/insane for the type to change based on how many rows are in the data frame. I'm not sure how flexible RJSONIO is, but it would be ideal if we could treat data frames, matrices, etc. different than atomic vectors and lists.

On Thu, Jan 24, 2013 at 12:18 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
>   I am sending data frames in JSON format to the browser client.
>
>   Usually a data frame is transferred as an JSON object of arrays.
>
>   In the special case where there is only one row, the JSON is an object of primitives
>
> This seems to be the default behaviour of TOJSONIO::toJSON
>
> > library(RJSONIO)
> > d=data.frame(a=1:2,b=letters[3:4])
> > cat(toJSON(d[1,]))
> {
>  "a": 1,
> "b": "c"
> }
> > cat(toJSON(d))
> {
>  "a": [ 1, 2 ],
> "b": [ "c", "d" ]
> }
>
> This transformation is equivalent to the 'drop'=T argument to the `[` operator, but
>
> I have addressed this on the server side using a function:
>
>     forceTableVector = function(table) {
>       lapply(as.list(table),as.list)
>     }
>
> But toJSON has an argument to do this:
>
> > asIs:
> > a logical value that, if TRUE causes R vectors of length 1 to be represented as arrays in JSON, but if FALSE to be represented as scalars, where appropriate (i.e. not the top level of the JSON content). This avoids having to explicitly mark sub-elements in an R object as being of class AsIs.
>
> > cat(toJSON(d[1,],asIs=T))
> {
>  "a": [ 1 ],
> "b": [ "c" ]
> }
>
> But perhaps shiny could make this transformation the default (especially while it's still beta!)
>
> Note that the asIS `I()` function does not help here:
>
> > cat(toJSON(I(d[1,])))
> {
>  "a": 1,
> "b": "c"
> }
>
> But an alternative formulation of the forceTable function is suggested by this:
>
> > cat(toJSON(lapply(d[1,],I)))
> {
>  "a": [ 1 ],
> "b": [ "c" ]
> }

>
> -Alex Brown
>

>

messages.subject: Re: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
On Tue, Feb 5, 2013 at 12:32 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> shiny.js uses a raw WebSocket by default, but the mechanism is extensible
> and Shiny Server extends it to use SockJS. Look at the HTML source of e.g.
> http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/diamonds/ and do a Find for SockJS and
> you'll see how it's done.
>
> I'm sure you will be able to proxy with nginx, other people (including me)
> have done it with Apache which also doesn't support proxying of ws and it
> works fine.

OHH now I see, the shiny-server invokes apps with the SockJSAdapter.R
wrapper, which injects some HTML/JS snippets.  Is there a reason it's
done that way?  (Rather than the more obvious thing of having the
framework return the full HTTP response and the Node.js server be a
dumb proxy).

I've written a similar server for R web apps.  What I did was just
have R open named pipes for request and response, sort of like CGI,
except the process persists across requests.  (Named pipes since the R
interpreter sometimes likes to spew stuff on stdout that you don't
intend.)

That way you can just use a vanilla R interpreter and you don't need
any special C extensions.  I just use netstrings to delimit requests
and responses.  Then the server, which is in Python, just reads from
those named pipes, and turns it into HTTP, like a CGI server would.

But what I was missing is the JavaScript/Bootstrap part, and I think
you've done a great job on that.  People were writing CGI-style R web
apps which can be tedious.

Anyway I'm sort of curious why the R process isn't just a plain HTTP
server rather than a Web Sockets server... I think the only advantage
of web sockets is doing server push?  It doesn't appear Shiny uses
that as all updates are in response to a user action.  On the other
side, I guess if you changed it to use pipes then people couldn't
develop without running a server as the parent of the R process.

Anyway I think we are about to become a paying RStudio customer from
what I understand (or are already), but I am not sure we could use a
Node.js server in our environment as it's quite specialized sys-admin
wise.

Andy

messages.body_plain:
Hi Amy,

Thanks, happy to share. I haven't found the time to get to grips with github yet (will soon) so here's the code :

UI.r
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("CCGsee : for viewing Clinical Commissioning Group data"),

  # Sidebar with controls
  sidebarPanel(

    uiOutput("choose_dataset"),

    selectInput("regionToPlot", "Plot which region ?",
                c("England" = "England",
                  "North" = "North",
                  "South" = "South",
                  "London" = "London",
                  "Midlands and East" = "Midlands and East"
                )),

    checkboxInput("addLegend", "add Legend to maps", TRUE), #var,name

    checkboxInput("addCodes", "add CCG codes to maps", FALSE), #var,name

    fileInput("file", "Load CCG data from a csv (must have CCG codes in column called CCG.code)", multiple=FALSE)
  ),

  mainPanel(

    h5("made at NHS HackDay Oxford 2013 by Andy South, Barry Rowlingson, Chris Martin and Rob Aldridge"),
    h5("contact sout...@gmail.com"),

    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Map", plotOutput("mapPlot")),
      tabPanel("Bubble Map", plotOutput("mapBubblesPlot")),
      tabPanel("Table", tableOutput("tablePlot")),
      tabPanel("Uploaded attribute data", tableOutput("filetable"))
      #tabPanel("demo Zoom map", includeHTML("olayer.html"))
    ) # end of tabsetPanel

  )
))

server.r
library(shiny)
library(rworldmap)

#load the data stored as files in the app folder
load('sPDF_CCG2.rda')

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  #for Barrys openLayers tab
  #addResourcePath("maps","maps")

  #creating a reactive variable for the map+data
  #so that whenever it is changed anything using it updates
  v <- reactiveValues( sPDF_CCGlocal = sPDF_CCG2 )

  # Drop-down selection box for columns
  output$choose_dataset <- reactiveUI(function() {

    selectInput("attributeToPlot", "Plot which attribute of CCGs ?", choices=getColumnNames())
  })

  # to provide a list of selected species based on input parameter
  getColumnNames <- reactive( function() {

    as.character( names(v$sPDF_CCGlocal)[c(3:ncol(v$sPDF_CCGlocal))])
    })

  #creating a command string for map plotting
  formulaText <- reactive(function() {

    trueOrFalse <- "FALSE"
    if (input$addLegend) trueOrFalse <- "TRUE"

    textOut <- paste("mapPolys(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot='",input$attributeToPlot,"', addLegend=",trueOrFalse,")",sep='') #, mapTitle=''

    if (input$addCodes)
    {
      textAdd <- "\ntext( coordinates(sPDF), sPDF$CCG.code, cex=0.8 )"
      textOut <- paste(textOut,textAdd)
    }

    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {
      textAdd <- paste("sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region =='", input$regionToPlot,"'), ]\n", sep='')
      textOut <- paste(textAdd, textOut)
    }

    textOut
    }) # end of formulaText()

  # Return the formula text for printing as a caption
  output$caption <- reactiveText(function() {
    formulaText()
  })

  # Generate a plot
  output$mapPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {

    if( length(input$attributeToPlot) == 0 )
    {
      plot.new <http://plot.new>()
      mtext("please wait for map to load (~20 seconds)",cex=2,col='purple')
    }

    #to stop it trying to plot map before an option has been chosen
    if( length(input$attributeToPlot) > 0 )
    {
      sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal

      oldpar <- par(mar=c(4,0,1,0)) # bottom, left, top, right
      eval(parse(text=formulaText()))

      mtext("map made using rworldmap", line=-2, side=1, adj=0, cex=0.8, col='purple')

      par(oldpar)
    }

  }) #end of mapPlot

  # bubble plot
  output$mapBubblesPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {

    sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal

    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {
      sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region == input$regionToPlot),]
    }

    oldpar <- par(mar=c(0,0,0,0)) # no gap therefore no room for axis
    mapBubbles(sPDF, nameZSize=input$attributeToPlot, fill=FALSE )

    if (input$addCodes)
    {
      text( coordinates(sPDF), sPDF$CCG.code, cex=0.8 )
    }

    mtext("map made using rworldmap", line=-2, side=1, adj=0, cex=0.8, col='purple')

    par(oldpar)
  }) #end of mapBubblesPlot

  # table
  output$tablePlot <- reactiveTable(function() {

    sPDF <- v$sPDF_CCGlocal

    if ( input$regionToPlot != 'England' )
    {
      sPDF <- sPDF[ which(sPDF$Region == input$regionToPlot),]
    }

    sPDF@data
  }) #end of tablePlot

  #called when user uploads a file
  output$filetable <- reactiveTable(function() {

    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }

    #cat("input$file=",input$file)
    print(paste("input$file$datapath=",input$file$datapath))

    dFuserData <- read.csv(input$file$datapath)

    #join data onto the map (changing the global sPDF in this function)
    #WEHAY! the isolate stops the reactive variable from setting up an infinite reactivity loop !
    sPDF_CCG3 <- joinData2Map(dF=dFuserData, nameMap=isolate(v$sPDF_CCGlocal), nameJoinIDMap='CCG.code', nameJoinColumnData='CCG.code')

    v$sPDF_CCGlocal <- sPDF_CCG3

    #what to print in the table
    dFuserData #just the user data

    #isolate stops an infinite loop
    #isolate(v$sPDF_CCGlocal@data) #the user data joined to the map attribute data

  }) # end of filetable

})

messages.subject: Re: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
On Tuesday, February 5, 2013, Andy Chu wrote:
> OHH now I see, the shiny-server invokes apps with the SockJSAdapter.R
> wrapper, which injects some HTML/JS snippets.  Is there a reason it's
> done that way?  (Rather than the more obvious thing of having the
> framework return the full HTTP response and the Node.js server be a
> dumb proxy).

Mostly, because there is no SockJS server for R (or C for that matter) and it didn't seem to be a good use of our resources to write one. The JS injection is pretty clean though and we will use it for other purposes in the future anyway.

> Anyway I'm sort of curious why the R process isn't just a plain HTTP
> server rather than a Web Sockets server... I think the only advantage
> of web sockets is doing server push?  It doesn't appear Shiny uses
> that as all updates are in response to a user action.

Server push is actually very important to us, updates can also be time based (invokeLater and reactiveTimer) and in the future we will also have reactive file watchers. This is important for, say, dashboard apps. You can also have a user in one session change a reactive value that causes other users' sessions to push new output to their browsers.

>   On the other
> side, I guess if you changed it to use pipes then people couldn't
> develop without running a server as the parent of the R process.

Yeah, the idea is that it is crazy easy to get started--just install.packages and you're ready to play around on localhost (assuming a modern browser). When it comes to deploying an app then we think it's tolerable that you have to install some additional software.

> Anyway I think we are about to become a paying RStudio customer from
> what I understand (or are already), but I am not sure we could use a
> Node.js server in our environment as it's quite specialized sys-admin
> wise.

Great! Do you mean node.js is not allowed by your sys admins, or that there are actual technical limitations (no Linux? very old Linux?)? Would love to hear more!

Thanks for the feedback!

--
Sent from my phone

messages.subject: Re: shiny does not evaluate the input$variable
messages.subject_clean: shiny does not evaluate the input$variable
messages.body_plain:
The issue is with the way you specify variables to ggplot. ggplot evaluates the contents of aes() in the context of the data frame, so normally you pass in the names of columns in the data, unquoted. If you want to pass in a variable that contains strings which _name_ the columns, you need aes_string(). For instance, these two are equivalent:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + geom_point()
ggplot(mtcars, aes_string(x="wt", y="mpg")) + geom_point()

So you want something like this:

ggplot(mpgData, aes_string(input$variable, "mpg")) + geom_point()

-Winston

The final version - wrapping the data frame list elements with I() is much faster than the list conversion function I supplied at the top.

Automatic strength reduction is one of my least favorite features of R - it causes constant pain.

-Alex.

On Jan 24, 2013, at 12:18 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
>   I am sending data frames in JSON format to the browser client.
>
>   Usually a data frame is transferred as an JSON object of arrays.
>
>   In the special case where there is only one row, the JSON is an object of primitives
>
> This seems to be the default behaviour of TOJSONIO::toJSON
>
> > library(RJSONIO)
> > d=data.frame(a=1:2,b=letters[3:4])
> > cat(toJSON(d[1,]))
> {
>  "a": 1,
> "b": "c"
> }
> > cat(toJSON(d))
> {
>  "a": [ 1, 2 ],
> "b": [ "c", "d" ]
> }
>
> This transformation is equivalent to the 'drop'=T argument to the `[` operator, but
>
> I have addressed this on the server side using a function:
>
>     forceTableVector = function(table) {
>       lapply(as.list(table),as.list)
>     }
>
> But toJSON has an argument to do this:
>
> > asIs:
> > a logical value that, if TRUE causes R vectors of length 1 to be represented as arrays in JSON, but if FALSE to be represented as scalars, where appropriate (i.e. not the top level of the JSON content). This avoids having to explicitly mark sub-elements in an R object as being of class AsIs.
>
> > cat(toJSON(d[1,],asIs=T))
> {
>  "a": [ 1 ],
> "b": [ "c" ]
> }
>
> But perhaps shiny could make this transformation the default (especially while it's still beta!)
>
> Note that the asIS `I()` function does not help here:
>
> > cat(toJSON(I(d[1,])))
> {
>  "a": 1,
> "b": "c"
> }
>
> But an alternative formulation of the forceTable function is suggested by this:
>
> > cat(toJSON(lapply(d[1,],I)))
> {
>  "a": [ 1 ],
> "b": [ "c" ]
> }
>
> -Alex Brown

require(shiny)

<script type="text/javascript">
google.load("visualization", "1", { packages:["geomap"] });
</script>
'
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("shiny with googleVis"),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(
    HTML(initGeomap),
    htmlOutput("gvis")
  )
  )
)

server.R:
require(shiny)
require(googleVis)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 output$gvis <- reactiveText(function(){

   G4 <- gvisGeoMap(Andrew, locationvar="LatLong", numvar="Speed_kt",
      hovervar="Category",
      options=list(height=350, region="US", dataMode="markers")
   )

   c(G4$html$chart,

       paste("\n<script type=\"text/javascript\">drawChart",

                           G4$chartid,"();</script>\n",sep="")
       )
 })
})

Best, Stefan

messages.subject: Re: "Translation" in HTML commands
messages.body_plain:
Probably the easiest way is to just execute those functions at an R console, wrapped in cat(as.character(...)). For example:

> cat(as.character(shiny::fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',
+           accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain'))))
<label>Choose CSV File</label>
<input id="file1" type="file" accept="text/csv,text/comma-separated-values,text/plain"/>

If you simply copy that resulting HTML and paste it into your own HTML document it should work identically.

messages.subject: advice on RS-DBI connections
messages.body_plain:
I've been struggling to come up with a good solution to maintain a database connection that can be reused across sessions without opening too many connections.  Declaring and opening the connection at the server level (outside session scope) seems to work fine, but then the connection times out overnight; if the sessions have to check the connection, and possibly replace it (using <<-), then I'm worried about a race condition between concurrent sessions (should I be?).  Previously I was having each session open a new connection, and then close it when finished, but when developing/debugging (read: errors), the connections would not get closed, and eventually I'd have to restart the server ("too many connections" error from RS-DBI).

Advice?

Thanks,
-Aaron

messages.subject: Re: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
>> Anyway I'm sort of curious why the R process isn't just a plain HTTP
>> server rather than a Web Sockets server... I think the only advantage
>> of web sockets is doing server push?  It doesn't appear Shiny uses
>> that as all updates are in response to a user action.
>
>
> Server push is actually very important to us, updates can also be time based
> (invokeLater and reactiveTimer) and in the future we will also have reactive
> file watchers. This is important for, say, dashboard apps. You can also have
> a user in one session change a reactive value that causes other users'
> sessions to push new output to their browsers.

Hm OK, but I can think of at least a dozen apps that people would want
to write that don't involve any kind of server push.  Does it seem
feasible to have an option for the R process to use plain HTTP?  In
that case those features would be disabled.

> Yeah, the idea is that it is crazy easy to get started--just
> install.packages and you're ready to play around on localhost (assuming a
> modern browser). When it comes to deploying an app then we think it's
> tolerable that you have to install some additional software.

Yeah that makes sense.

>> Anyway I think we are about to become a paying RStudio customer from
>> what I understand (or are already), but I am not sure we could use a
>> Node.js server in our environment as it's quite specialized sys-admin
>> wise.
>
>
> Great! Do you mean node.js is not allowed by your sys admins, or that there
> are actual technical limitations (no Linux? very old Linux?)? Would love to
> hear more!

We are not running any node.js right now, although that may be
surmountable.  But more important is custom auth, and also monitoring.
 Our environment is pretty specialized (and depending on the situation
Linux may be old too).

Some people are also concerned about security, since R is not really
meant to be exposed to the web.  It's C code is definitely not
designed with that in mind :)  So some kind of sandboxing of R
processes may also be desired.

Overall it seems like proxying the R process ourselves is the most
realistic approach, which is why I was asking about HTTP.   Any
comments on that appreciated.

thanks,
Andy

messages.subject: Re: Shiny without web sockets?
messages.body_plain:
> Does it seem feasible to have an option for the R process to use plain HTTP?

That doesn't seem like something we'd prioritize anytime soon, sorry. It would mostly benefit people who are implementing their own Shiny Server, in which case emulating websockets over HTTP is not a particularly hard problem (SockJS, socket.io <http://socket.io>, Kaazing, or just do your own Comet based impl).

> Overall it seems like proxying the R process ourselves is the most
> realistic approach, which is why I was asking about HTTP.   Any
> comments on that appreciated.

Sandboxing, custom auth, and monitoring is all coming for the enterprise version of Shiny Server later this year. If you don't want to use Node.js you'll basically have to rewrite everything we did (and will do) for Shiny Server, but in C (or whatever). In other words you'd have to really, really not want to use Node to make that a worthwhile tradeoff!

If you build Node.js from source then it's possible even pretty old versions of Linux would be supported. I can't say we've tested on anything older than a couple of years though (CentOS 5, Ubuntu 10.04). I do think it kind of unlikely that there'd be a setup that'd be able to support R 2.15 but not Node, as the latter has FAR fewer dependencies.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Error
messages.body_plain:
It's possible your computer is configured to use a proxy server for all HTTP requests, including those to localhost. If so, your web browser and/or OS should allow you to bypass the proxy for certain hosts, and you should add localhost and/or 127.0.0.1 and/or 127.0.1.1 to that list. Do a google search for "bypass proxy" plus your browser and/or OS and you should be able to find a lot of instructions for doing that.

You could make the navbar itself a Shiny input (i.e. write an InputBinding for Bootstrap navbars), whose value is the most recently selected menu item plus a unique number (the latter to prevent selecting the same item twice in a row from being a no-op the second time).

Maybe something like this:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/4735365

You'd make sure the div.navbar itself had an id attribute, then all of the <a> tags that want to be Shiny inputs would also need id attributes (you could change that though to refer to a different attribute, maybe data-value instead).

Note that I haven't tested this. Seems like it should be close to correct though.

messages.body_plain:
Vincent, sorry for not answering this earlier. We're not sure actionButton as written has the right interface, and once we add it to Shiny it becomes much harder to change. If I were you I'd just copy the R and JS code right into your app.

There's not a great reason shinyIncubator isn't on CRAN though, other than it being kind of a pain to put things on CRAN and also to update them :)

If you end up doing a bunch of custom code that you need across projects, you could do your own package for your Shiny extensions--that'd be really cool!

messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
messages.body_plain:
Wow, you'd have to restart the server? Are you sure just restarting the R process wouldn't fix it? If the latter is true, then perhaps you could write your own wrapper around shiny::runApp that would wrap it in a withCallingHandlers call, and in the case of exception, close the connection.

BTW, how were you able to tell when a Shiny session is finished?

On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 9:18 AM, Aaron Mackey <ajma...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I've been struggling to come up with a good solution to maintain a database connection that can be reused across sessions without opening too many connections.  Declaring and opening the connection at the server level (outside session scope) seems to work fine, but then the connection times out overnight; if the sessions have to check the connection, and possibly replace it (using <<-), then I'm worried about a race condition between concurrent sessions (should I be?).  Previously I was having each session open a new connection, and then close it when finished, but when developing/debugging (read: errors), the connections would not get closed, and eventually I'd have to restart the server ("too many connections" error from RS-DBI).
>
> Advice?
>
> Thanks,
> -Aaron

messages.subject: problem integrating with cytoscape.js
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to integrate shiny with cytoscape.js, basing my code on Jeff Allen's nice d3 example here:

http://trestletechnology.net/2012/12/reconstruct-gene-networks/

I'm running into a problem that when I click on a node in my cytoscape.js network, I should see a console message telling me which node I've clicked on, but instead cytoscape tells me that I've clicked on the background of the graph, not a node.

Here you can see that problem in action:
http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/

Open a javascript console. Wait for the graph to setle down, click on a node. You'll see "click on background" in the console.

Here is how it is supposed to work, a miminal example that is just a plain static HTML file, no shiny involved:

http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/standalone.html

If you click on a node there, you'll see something like "clicked on X3055 " in the console.

So, I started looking for differences between those two files. I took the source obtained by running "View source" on
http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/

and started commenting things out until it worked (at some point I also needed to hardcode the data so it wasn't coming from shiny).

The result is:

http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/all.html

If you click on a node, you'll see its name in the console. Yay!

So the last thing I had commented out was:

<div class="span8">

And maybe I am mistaken, but that did not seem to have a closing div?

Anyway, I thought I had solved the problem. So I went back to

http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/

took the source of it and put it in a new file and just removed that span8 div. The result should be:

http://cloud.bioconductor.org:3838/cyshiny/stillbroken.html

but that doesn't display for some reason in my shiny server. So you'll have to download the shiny app and run it locally:

https://s3.amazonaws.com/cyshiny/cyshiny.tar.gz

Then you can see the problem here:

http://localhost:8100/stillbroken.html

Clicking on a node is still broken and the border around the graph is in the wrong place.

At this point I am lost....it looks like shiny is putting something in the UI it generates that is breaking the graph's ability to know where you are when you click in it.

Can someone help?

Thanks!
Dan

messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
messages.body_plain:
How do I restart the R process without restarting the shiny-server?  Reloading the page reloads the server.R code, but doesn't restart the R process (?)

Regardless, how should I orchestrate things to keep from having to restart anything?

re: <<- and race conditions -- is this a general concern? said another way, are individual sessions run in parallel threads, or only serially (new sessions "block" or wait until earlier session responses are completed)?  It's not clear to me what the UML sequence diagram looks like with stateful websockets ...

and no, I don't know when a session finishes; what I meant to say is that I previously had each function that needed a connection open a new one, and close it when finished; but errors in between caused orphaned connections to be left open.  I could clean up my database access routines to use tryCatch to more cleanly exit without leaving orphans, but it still seems wasteful to constantly re-open database connections, when one "master" connection should suffice -- if I could just keep it from timing out (a RS-DBI question, I suppose).

-Aaron

--
Aaron J. Mackey, PhD
Assistant Professor
Center for Public Health Genomics
University of Virginia
ama...@virginia.edu
http://www.cphg.virginia.edu/mackey

> Wow, you'd have to restart the server? Are you sure just restarting the R process wouldn't fix it? If the latter is true, then perhaps you could write your own wrapper around shiny::runApp that would wrap it in a withCallingHandlers call, and in the case of exception, close the connection.
>
> BTW, how were you able to tell when a Shiny session is finished?
>
>
> On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 9:18 AM, Aaron Mackey <ajma...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I've been struggling to come up with a good solution to maintain a database connection that can be reused across sessions without opening too many connections.  Declaring and opening the connection at the server level (outside session scope) seems to work fine, but then the connection times out overnight; if the sessions have to check the connection, and possibly replace it (using <<-), then I'm worried about a race condition between concurrent sessions (should I be?).  Previously I was having each session open a new connection, and then close it when finished, but when developing/debugging (read: errors), the connections would not get closed, and eventually I'd have to restart the server ("too many connections" error from RS-DBI).
> >
> > Advice?

> > Thanks,

messages.subject: Shiny Server on EC2
messages.body_plain:
All,

I had been working on setting up a private Shiny Server on EC2 and thought I'd go ahead and document the process in case anyone else might benefit. I installed it on Amazon's custom Linux AMI, which required slight modification of how I had installed R and used Upstart previously.

The whole process is documented here: http://trestletechnology.net/2013/02/deploying-shiny-server-on-amazon-ec2/ , or you can just boot up the AMI directly; the name is "ShinyServer."

Let me know if you have any suggestions for the setup guide! I know I went a bit nuclear on the X libraries, but that was leftover from some work I was doing with RGL which did require a litany of X packages. I may go clean those up on the AMI in the future...

Jeff

Well, that was interesting. I tracked it down to a bug in Cytoscape.js and went to go submit a pull request, but on their master branch this is already fixed.

https://github.com/cytoscape/cytoscape.js/commit/c03ec996a258963dae7da83a246ae3de3c36e1f9 (line 752-3)

With that one line changed from parentNode to offsetParent, the problem goes away.

messages.subject: Shiny-server and x11
messages.body_plain:
Hi, shiny-ers!

We've managed to install and configure the shine-server to run on our linux server. My scripts run fine and the UI page is presented properly, but the graphics do not show - instead an error is reported:

> ERROR: *X11 is not available.

We tracked this down to the lack of a proper X-server on the machine, so we configured shiny-server to print  using a virtual
framebuffer X (Xvfb). We modified the shiny-server startup script to run
Xvfb and export DISPLAY=:3.1 - this worked fine for other softwares running on the machine.
>
> ws1 ~ # ps -ef | grep Xvfb
> shiny     5205     1  0 15:10 ?        00:00:00 /usr/bin/Xvfb :3 -screen 1
> 800x600x16

Even when I explicitly defined the DISPLAY variable in the server.R like this:
> Sys.setenv(DISPLAY = ":3.1")
It didn't work and the error permains. In a last ditch attempt, I even tried to set
> options(bitmapType="cairo")
which I saw was a suggestion for a somewheat related problem in another thread.

messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
messages.body_plain:
Oh, I misunderstood. I thought you meant you had to restart the database server.

All R code in a process runs single-threaded. This is just an inherent feature/limitation of R itself. So you should be able to structure your code so that race conditions are not too much of a concern. Probably the easiest thing to do then would be to create a function in global.R that does something like the following:

getConnection <- function() {
  if (!exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv) || (Sys.time() - .connOpened) > 600) {
    if (exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv))
      closeConnection(.connection)
    .connection <<- openNewConnection()
    .connOpened <<- Sys.time()
  }
  return(.connection)
}

Basically it returns a cached connection, unless a certain amount of time has passed, in which case it closes the existing connection and opens a new one. Or instead of basing it on time, you could run a trivial query and see if it succeeds.

On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 5:11 PM, Aaron Mackey <ama...@virginia.edu> wrote:
> How do I restart the R process without restarting the shiny-server?  Reloading the page reloads the server.R code, but doesn't restart the R process (?)
>
> Regardless, how should I orchestrate things to keep from having to restart anything?
>
> re: <<- and race conditions -- is this a general concern? said another way, are individual sessions run in parallel threads, or only serially (new sessions "block" or wait until earlier session responses are completed)?  It's not clear to me what the UML sequence diagram looks like with stateful websockets ...
>
> and no, I don't know when a session finishes; what I meant to say is that I previously had each function that needed a connection open a new one, and close it when finished; but errors in between caused orphaned connections to be left open.  I could clean up my database access routines to use tryCatch to more cleanly exit without leaving orphans, but it still seems wasteful to constantly re-open database connections, when one "master" connection should suffice -- if I could just keep it from timing out (a RS-DBI question, I suppose).
>
> -Aaron
>
> --
> Aaron J. Mackey, PhD
> Assistant Professor
> Center for Public Health Genomics
> University of Virginia
> ama...@virginia.edu
> http://www.cphg.virginia.edu/mackey
>
>
> On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 7:12 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > Wow, you'd have to restart the server? Are you sure just restarting the R process wouldn't fix it? If the latter is true, then perhaps you could write your own wrapper around shiny::runApp that would wrap it in a withCallingHandlers call, and in the case of exception, close the connection.
> >
> > BTW, how were you able to tell when a Shiny session is finished?
> >
> >
> > On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 9:18 AM, Aaron Mackey <ajma...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I've been struggling to come up with a good solution to maintain a database connection that can be reused across sessions without opening too many connections.  Declaring and opening the connection at the server level (outside session scope) seems to work fine, but then the connection times out overnight; if the sessions have to check the connection, and possibly replace it (using <<-), then I'm worried about a race condition between concurrent sessions (should I be?).  Previously I was having each session open a new connection, and then close it when finished, but when developing/debugging (read: errors), the connections would not get closed, and eventually I'd have to restart the server ("too many connections" error from RS-DBI).

I was thinking you could add an R function "select2Input", that is *very* roughly:

select2Input <- function(inputId, ...) {
  tagList(
    tags$script(src="select2.js"),
    selectInput(inputId=inputId, ...),
    tags$script(paste("$(function() { $('#", inputId, "').select2(); });", sep=""))
  )
}

messages.body_plain:
Hi, This has probably been covered, but use a trick to prevent dynamic UI from being re-rendered each time the user selects something from a drop-down:

The user selects one or two strings from the drop-down
I render different tabs for 'one' vs 'two'
the actual strings can change while still being only one of them (or two of them).

e.g. the user selected Jan, or Feb or March etc.
or the user selected Jan AND Feb or Jan AND March.

I created a function like this :

countMonths <- reactive(function() {
  length(input$months)
})

And thus the reactive UI stays the same unless the user decides to select MORE (1->2) or LESS (2->1) months.

This works because reactives cache their result, and if it's still the same, then the parent function is not triggered.

If I replace the call to countMonths() with a number (e.g. 1) in my reactive UI function, then the reactive UI (correctly) doesn't update.
If I replace the contents of countMonths with just return(1) then the reactive UI (correctly) doesn't update.

However, this no longer seems to work - each time the user moves from Jan->Feb, the reactive UI gets re-run and blows away my tab position (not to mention rendering the output twice - once for the month update and then again to move to the default tab).

I did update shiny from CRAN yesterday but I don't know if that's the issue.

Does this seem familiar?

Is there some way I can see why shiny decides to re-trigger the reactiveUI function?

Does the new lazy work fix this?

Why did I think it used to work?

-Alex

messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
messages.body_plain:
Here's what I ended up with in global.R

library(RMySQL)

getConnection <- function(group) {

  if (!exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv)) {
    .connection <<- dbConnect(MySQL(), group=group)
  } else if (class(try(dbGetQuery(.connection, "SELECT 1"))) == "try-error") {
    dbDisconnect(.connection)
    .connection <<- dbConnect(MySQL(), group=group)
  }

  return(.connection)
}

Thanks again,
-Aaron

--
Aaron J. Mackey, PhD
Assistant Professor
Center for Public Health Genomics
University of Virginia
ama...@virginia.edu
http://www.cphg.virginia.edu/mackey

On Fri, Feb 8, 2013 at 6:00 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> Oh, I misunderstood. I thought you meant you had to restart the database server.
>
> All R code in a process runs single-threaded. This is just an inherent feature/limitation of R itself. So you should be able to structure your code so that race conditions are not too much of a concern. Probably the easiest thing to do then would be to create a function in global.R that does something like the following:
>
> getConnection <- function() {
>   if (!exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv) || (Sys.time() - .connOpened) > 600) {
>     if (exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv))
>       closeConnection(.connection)
>     .connection <<- openNewConnection()
>     .connOpened <<- Sys.time()
>   }
>   return(.connection)
> }
>
> Basically it returns a cached connection, unless a certain amount of time has passed, in which case it closes the existing connection and opens a new one. Or instead of basing it on time, you could run a trivial query and see if it succeeds.
>
>
> On Thu, Feb 7, 2013 at 5:11 PM, Aaron Mackey <ama...@virginia.edu> wrote:

> > re: <<- and race conditions -- is this a general concern? said another way, are individual sessions run in parallel threads, or only serially (new sessions "block" or wait until earlier session responses are completed)?  It's not clear to me what the UML sequence diagram looks like with stateful websockets ...
> >
> > and no, I don't know when a session finishes; what I meant to say is that I previously had each function that needed a connection open a new one, and close it when finished; but errors in between caused orphaned connections to be left open.  I could clean up my database access routines to use tryCatch to more cleanly exit without leaving orphans, but it still seems wasteful to constantly re-open database connections, when one "master" connection should suffice -- if I could just keep it from timing out (a RS-DBI question, I suppose).

messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

It is related to the reactive-function-lazy-evaluation change. The property you are describing, let's call "insulation". Shiny reactive funcs used to have insulation but not laziness. Now they have laziness but not insulation.  However, there is a different technique you can use now to get insulation.

v <- reactiveValues(countMonths=0)
observe(function() {
  v$countMonths <- length(input$months)
})

>From your reactiveUI, use v$countMonths to read the value instead of countMonths().

Essentially, observe provides the eagerness and going through reactiveValues provides the insulation.

output$graphBlock <- reactiveUI(function() {

  panels <- Map(
        function(plotName)tagList(h4(plotSpec[[plotName]]$name),div()),

 # construct the tabs as an argument list

  # now build the tabs.
  Tabs=do.call(tabsetPanel,paneltags)

The easy way to avoir it is to use the British spelling for the plyr version: 'summarise', instead of 'summarize'.

messages.subject: Re: Debugging invalidation
messages.body_plain:
No, we don't have a dependency graph. I don't think a dependency graph will help in this case (but you're more than welcome to try to prove otherwise). We avoid over-reactivity in most cases through lazy evaluation and deferred execution of observers, but not in the case of setting reactiveValues. When you go through reactiveValues, you're exiting the reactive framework and coming back in (since setting a reactive value is something that happens outside of the reactive graph--it's unintuitive but true).

Can you tell me what reactiveVal$A/B and the reactiveUI actually represent, so we can talk about whether there's another way to structure things?

messages.subject_clean: numbers received by shiny output js come across with different values
messages.body_plain:
Looks like the position is being changed by cytoscape (scaling to the canvas size or whatever, I imagine). Turns out console.log calls are asynchronous, and although you're logging before the data is changed, the objects are passed by reference so by the time they're actually written, the values are different.
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8747421/javascript-console-prints-assigned-value-of-variable-before-it-has-been-assigned

You can confirm this by replacing console.log(data) with console.log(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(data))), which will copy the data.

The tabsets/tabs depend on Bootstrap <http://getbootstrap.com>. You need these lines:

  <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="shared/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css"/>

  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"/>
  <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="shared/bootstrap/css/bootstrap-responsive.min.css"/>

(The last line is optional)

messages.subject_clean: My shiny-server set-up : Shiny-Server no sudo patch
messages.body_plain:
This is great. It might make sense to have a run_as value that implies that the current user should be used (and abort with an error if the server is running as root).

On Fri, Feb 8, 2013 at 3:41 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I don't have sudo access on my webservers, so I needed to run as the web user:
>
> The patch to allow this in shiny-server can be found here:
> https://github.com/alexbbrown/shiny-server/commit/15c54786766b927937d84cea850c87deada53088
>
> The config:
> run_as scbldmnr;
>
> server {
>   listen 8100;
>
>   location / {
>     log_dir /infrastructure/shiny/log;
>     site_dir /infrastructure/shiny/www;
>   }
> }
>
> Running under apache:
> I then configured apache to proxy a sub-path onto the node.js server:
>
> ProxyRequests off
>
> <Proxy *>
>     Order deny,allow
>     Allow from all
> </Proxy>
>
> <Location /sims/>
>     ProxyPass http://localhost:8100/sims/
>     ProxyPassReverse http://localhost:8100/sims/
> </Location>
>
> Hope this helps someone.

>
> -Alex

messages.subject: Select2 and DT_Bootstrap in one Shiny web app
messages.subject_clean: Select2 and DT_Bootstrap in one Shiny web app
messages.body_plain:
This is a follow-up to at least three group discussions about extending existing Javascript controls within the Shiny framework, namely Select2 and DataTable (Bootstrap). I wanted to write this to give something back to the group as so many others have helped significantly grow the Shiny tools.

This is a summary of the following discussions:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/Fonr8vtOfpk
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/T4NL74DtDdI
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/K8LiWIM1ras

To begin with, I am a total Javascript and CSS newbie, so anyone that has significant skills in these areas, please feel free to make corrections with this post. If you are reading this and have no knowledge of Javascript or CSS and want to utilize these tools quickly in your Shiny webapp, then this might be quite helpful to you.

To be honest, the way I have been able to get these tools to work within Shiny feels a little brittle, but they work. Very little of what i have done is original work or code. The DataTable code was plagiarized from an earlier post by Haider Ali and the Select2 code was plagiarized from a recent post by Joe Cheng. I just want to give credit where credit is due.

One thing to note in the DataTable implementation. I hardcoded the value 'table' in the "$(document).ready" function at the end of the DT_Bootstrap.js file. I think this means all tables in the app will default to DT_Bootstrap tables, but I am not sure. I also extended the reactiveDataTable function to include the ID/name of the table as a parameter. The DataTable functionality also requires the xtable and stringer packages.

This example also uses the "actionButton" from the ShinyIncubator package.

To run the example, just unzip and issue a "runApp" command to the directory.

messages.subject: Re: Downloading plots using downloadHandler()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gabriel -

I've modified the 10_download example, and this works:

  output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      paste(input$dataset, Sys.time(), '.png', sep='')
    },

    content = function(file) {

      png(file, width = 980, height = 400, units = "px", pointsize = 12, bg = "white", res = NA)

      plot(1,1)

      dev.off()
    },
    contentType = 'image/png'
  )

Note a couple differences:
* No need to do `y <- plot(1,1)` or `print(y)` for plot(), though something like that is needed if you use ggplot().

* Use `filename = function()` instead of `filename <- function()`. The latter may have worked, but only because it uses positional matching. It would also assign values to `function` and `content` in the parent environment. This will illustrate:

foo <- function(a, b) {
  cat("a=", a, "  b=", b, "\n", sep="")
}

foo(a <- 1, b = 2)
# a=1  b=2

a
# 1
b
# Error: object 'b' not found

# Reverse b and a
foo(b <- 1, a <- 2)
# a=1  b=2

messages.subject: Re: HTML file from server.R to ui.R
messages.subject_clean: HTML file from server.R to ui.R
messages.body_plain:
Use reactiveUI to achieve what you want. Here is a rough sketch of what to insert in server.R and ui.R. So whenever, the user selects a different model, the reactiveUI will trigger HTML to be included from the appropriate file.

=========
server.R
=========

output$showfile <- reactiveUI(function(){
  file_to_show = switch(input$model, 'file1.html', 'file2.html')
  includeHTML(file_to_show)
})

==========
ui.R
==========

uiOutput("showfile")

messages.subject: ActionButton or SubmitButton
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I would like to build an app which takes parameters from the UI and, when the user click on a button, the server executes a homemade function. Finally, i have to plot the results.
I do not need the reactive function since I want to use the server side as a computation machine.

I tried to do such app based on the tutorial of Shiny but the problem is that the computation in my function begins immediately, even before I clicked on the submitButton.
 I do not know how to wait that the button is clicked to execute myFunction.

######UI.R code :
library(shiny)
library(shinyIncubator)

# Define UI for miles per gallon application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("perTurbo Classification"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select the variable to plot against mpg
  # and to specify whether outliers should be included
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:",
                choices = c("at_chloro", "tan2009r1", "dunkley2006")),

    submitButton("Execute"),

  ),

  # Show the caption and plot of the requested variable against mpg
  # Show a tabset that includes a plot, summary, and table view
  # of the generated distribution
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot"))
)
  )
))

###### server.R code

# Define server logic required to plot various variables against mpg
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

   #
  paramInput <- function() {
    list("dataset" = input$dataset )

  }

  output$plot <- reactivePlot(function() {
    theDataSet <- datasetInput()
    foo <- myFunction(theDataset)
   plot(foo)
  })

})

Thanks for your help

Sam

username: ramnathv
repo        : testshiny

deploy:

You could use RStudio server on glimmer and create a project for your app: http://glimmer.rstudio.com:8787/

> * some facility to push the files I've uploaded to my server from this server to the respective shiny app folder. I know that R can read files from HTTP URLs but, ideally, I would like it to be a secure connection so I don't have confidential data lying around publicly on the web

That's very clever, Ramnath.

I think we should add an <input type="hidden"> binding to Shiny. So you could just set the hidden value, rather than a visible field and then hiding it.

I hesitate to share this with you, but there is another way, that is not documented and may not be supported in the future as it breaks some collaboration features we were hoping to get to one day. You can call Shiny.onInputChange(name, value) and that will act as if that control exists and was changed. However it can't be used while the page is loading; the Shiny client code must have fully initialized first.

messages.subject: Upcoming changes to Shiny API
messages.body_plain:
Hello Shiny users -

In the development version of Shiny on github, we've merged in a branch that makes some changes to the API. Your old code should continue to work, but it will result in messages about deprecated usage being printed to the console. There will be a bit of short-term pain in switching to the new API, but we think it's worthwhile, because the new interface is somewhat simpler, and because it offers a better mapping between the names and concepts.

If you like being on the cutting edge, please install this version on your local machine and test it out on your apps!
  library('devtools')
  install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

You can also install it on your account on Glimmer by connecting to RStudio server and installing from there. If you do so, then your apps will use your installed version of Shiny; if not, they will continue to use the system's installed version of Shiny, 3.1. (You may have to put 'library(shiny)' at the top your app's .R files for this to work, though.)

Here's what has changed:

* `reactive()` takes expressions as input, instead of functions. Here's an example:
  # Old style
  reactive(function() { ... })
  # New style
  reactive({ ... })

* `observe() also takes expressions instead of functions:
  # Old style
  observe(function() { ... })
  # New style
  observe({ ... })

* `reactiveText`, `reactivePlot`, and so on, have been replaced with `renderText`, `renderPlot`, etc. They also now take expressions instead of functions.
  # Old style
  reactiveText(function() { ... })
  # New style
  renderText({ ... })

If for some reason you want to save an unevaluated expression in a variable and then give it to, `reactive()`, `renderText()`, and so on, you can quote the expression and then use the quote=TRUE option:
  my_expr <- quote({ input$num + 1 })
  renderText(my_expr, quote=TRUE)

This should cover most use cases, although it's possible you might still run into some hurdles if you're doing tricky stuff with Shiny. If you still have problems migrating, please feel free to ask about it on this mailing list.

When we release the next version of Shiny, we'll also update the tutorial pages to reflect the new API.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Upcoming changes to Shiny API
messages.body_plain:
Seems to be working just fine. Changed reactive to render where needed and removed 'function()'.

On Thursday, February 14, 2013 12:21:08 PM UTC-8, Winston Chang wrote:
> Hello Shiny users -
>
> In the development version of Shiny on github, we've merged in a branch that makes some changes to the API. Your old code should continue to work, but it will result in messages about deprecated usage being printed to the console. There will be a bit of short-term pain in switching to the new API, but we think it's worthwhile, because the new interface is somewhat simpler, and because it offers a better mapping between the names and concepts.
>
> If you like being on the cutting edge, please install this version on your local machine and test it out on your apps!
>   library('devtools')
>   install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')
>
> You can also install it on your account on Glimmer by connecting to RStudio server and installing from there. If you do so, then your apps will use your installed version of Shiny; if not, they will continue to use the system's installed version of Shiny, 3.1. (You may have to put 'library(shiny)' at the top your app's .R files for this to work, though.)
>
>
> Here's what has changed:
>
> * `reactive()` takes expressions as input, instead of functions. Here's an example:
>   # Old style
>   reactive(function() { ... })
>   # New style
>   reactive({ ... })
>
> * `observe() also takes expressions instead of functions:
>   # Old style
>   observe(function() { ... })
>   # New style
>   observe({ ... })
>
> * `reactiveText`, `reactivePlot`, and so on, have been replaced with `renderText`, `renderPlot`, etc. They also now take expressions instead of functions.
>   # Old style
>   reactiveText(function() { ... })
>   # New style
>   renderText({ ... })
>
>
>
> If for some reason you want to save an unevaluated expression in a variable and then give it to, `reactive()`, `renderText()`, and so on, you can quote the expression and then use the quote=TRUE option:
>   my_expr <- quote({ input$num + 1 })
>   renderText(my_expr, quote=TRUE)
>
>
> This should cover most use cases, although it's possible you might still run into some hurdles if you're doing tricky stuff with Shiny. If you still have problems migrating, please feel free to ask about it on this mailing list.
>
>
> When we release the next version of Shiny, we'll also update the tutorial pages to reflect the new API.
>
> -Winston
>

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
messages.body_plain:
Here is one way to get this workflow functional.

1. Create a Dropbox folder (say myshinyapp)
2. Add ui.R, server.R and other files for your app.
3. Share dropbox folder with your collaborators.
4. Add a makefile to your repo

   username: ignacio
   appname: myshinyapp
  deploy-glimmer:
   rsync -avz --delete . $(username)@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

5. If you want git and github as well
   (a) Initialize Repo, Add Files and Commit

       $ git init && git add . && git commit -am 'initial commit'

 (b) Add these lines to your makefile

    deploy-github:
      git push g...@github.com:$(username)/$(appname)

This will ensure that even if your coauthor's mess up, your work is backed up on Dropbox which saves versions. Moreover, everyone gets to work from their Desktop ensuring offline access. messages.subject: Re: Upcoming changes to Shiny API
messages.body_plain:
Great! I know you've been working on some pretty complex Shiny apps, so it's good to hear that you haven't hit any bugs with the new changes.

-Winston

On Thu, Feb 14, 2013 at 7:26 PM, Vincent <mostly.ha...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Seems to be working just fine. Changed reactive to render where needed and removed 'function()'.
>
>
> On Thursday, February 14, 2013 12:21:08 PM UTC-8, Winston Chang wrote:
> > Hello Shiny users -
> >
> > In the development version of Shiny on github, we've merged in a branch that makes some changes to the API. Your old code should continue to work, but it will result in messages about deprecated usage being printed to the console. There will be a bit of short-term pain in switching to the new API, but we think it's worthwhile, because the new interface is somewhat simpler, and because it offers a better mapping between the names and concepts.
> >
> > If you like being on the cutting edge, please install this version on your local machine and test it out on your apps!
> >   library('devtools')
> >   install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')
> >
> > You can also install it on your account on Glimmer by connecting to RStudio server and installing from there. If you do so, then your apps will use your installed version of Shiny; if not, they will continue to use the system's installed version of Shiny, 3.1. (You may have to put 'library(shiny)' at the top your app's .R files for this to work, though.)
> >
> >
> > Here's what has changed:
> >
> > * `reactive()` takes expressions as input, instead of functions. Here's an example:
> >   # Old style
> >   reactive(function() { ... })
> >   # New style
> >   reactive({ ... })
> >
> > * `observe() also takes expressions instead of functions:
> >   # Old style
> >   observe(function() { ... })
> >   # New style
> >   observe({ ... })
> >
> > * `reactiveText`, `reactivePlot`, and so on, have been replaced with `renderText`, `renderPlot`, etc. They also now take expressions instead of functions.
> >   # Old style
> >   reactiveText(function() { ... })
> >   # New style
> >   renderText({ ... })
> >
> >
> >
> > If for some reason you want to save an unevaluated expression in a variable and then give it to, `reactive()`, `renderText()`, and so on, you can quote the expression and then use the quote=TRUE option:
> >   my_expr <- quote({ input$num + 1 })
> >   renderText(my_expr, quote=TRUE)
> >
> >
> > This should cover most use cases, although it's possible you might still run into some hurdles if you're doing tricky stuff with Shiny. If you still have problems migrating, please feel free to ask about it on this mailing list.
> >
> >
> > When we release the next version of Shiny, we'll also update the tutorial pages to reflect the new API.
> >
> > -Winston

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server API including file transfer?
messages.body_plain:
The custom web interface sounds like going through a lot of effort to have a worse editing experience, not to mention being completely unable to deal with merge conflicts (i.e. what happens if two people are editing at the same time?). By moving away from RStudio or something like it, you're also losing tab completion, help, source code execution, R prompt, etc. Are you certain your collaborators need that much protection? Wouldn't it be easier to just explain to them that they shouldn't edit any files but ui.R and server.R?

On Fri, Feb 15, 2013 at 6:02 AM, Ignacio Perez Hallerbach <ignacio.pere...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Joe and Ramnath,
>
> thanks again for your replies. My apologies for getting into this again but I have 2 further questions. I understand that Ramnath's suggestion still requires me to do the development locally and run at least one command (i.e. the "make" command to run the makefile) manually from the command line. If we assume that I do not want to do that at all, but rather, I would like the workflow to be as follows, would this be possible?
>
> (1) Collaborators use a custom web interface (with less functionality than RStudio but similar to Yihui's notebook where only one file is edited at a time) to edit the server.R and ui.R files (e.g. when they click save, the content of the text boxes is saved in the files)
> (2) The two files server.R and ui.R are pushed to my GitHub repository via the GitHub API
> (3) Using a Service Hook on my repo, the ShinyApp server is notified of a new push to my repo
> (4) The ShinyApp server reacts by pulling the updated files into my respective shiny app directory
> (5) The updated ShinyApp is ready
>
> Is there any way of making this workflow happen? Moreover, re (1), is there a web-based open source R editor out there that is similar to Yihui's notebook and has less functionality than RStudio, i.e. allows to modify exactly one file at a time?
>
>
> Thanks so much again! Best,
>
> Ignacio

messages.body_plain:
The block needs to be in sidebarPanel. This should work:

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that plots random distributions
shinyUI(

  pageWithSidebar(

    # Application title
    headerPanel("Clustering results"),

    # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
    sidebarPanel(

      tags$head(

        tags$style(type="text/css", "select { max-width: 200px; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", "textarea { max-width: 185px; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", ".jslider { max-width: 200px; }"),
        tags$style(type='text/css', ".well { max-width: 310px; }"),
        tags$style(type='text/css', ".span4 { max-width: 310px; }")
      ),

      helpText("There are 615 experiments\n",
               "and 230595 peptides.",
               "minExp = 2, minPep = 2."),

      selectInput("k","Method for choosing k for SVD:",
                  choices = c("Akaike information criteria (k = )", "Amended description length (k = )",
                              "Percentange of var. explained = 0.5 (k = )","Percentange of var. explained = 0.8 (k = )",
                              "Percentange of var. explained = 0.95 (k = )")
      )
    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Heatmap", plotOutput("heatmap",width = "800px", height = "800px")),

        #tabPanel("Heatmap", plotOutput("heatmap",width = "1000px", height = "900px")),
        tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary"))
      )
    )
  )
)

Dear!

When I run my loop, I should see the red line over time. However, I just visualize the final graph, ie I do not see the loop running.

Why?

ui.R

library(shiny)
# Define UI for slider demo application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

                        #  Application title
                        headerPanel("Sliders"),

                        # Sidebar with sliders that demonstrate various available options
                        sidebarPanel(
                                     # Número de lançamentos
                                     numericInput("flips", "Lançamentos:",1000),

                                     # Decimal interval with step value
                                     numericInput("p.head", "Probabilidade:",0.5,
                                                  min = 0, max = 1),

                                     # Specification of range within an interval
                                     numericInput("interval", "Intervalo:",0.01),

                                     submitButton(text = "Iniciar"),

                                     checkboxInput(inputId = "show.coin",
                                                   label = strong("Mostrar moeda"),
                                                   value = FALSE)
                                     ),
                        mainPanel(
                        plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot", height = "300px")
                        )
                     ))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(plotrix)
# Define server logic for slider examples
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

            output$main_plot <- reactivePlot(function() {

                                             res <- rbinom(n = input$flips, size = 1, prob = input$p.head)
                                             n.trials <- seq(1, input$flips)
                                             cum.s <- cumsum(res)
                                             cum.p <- cum.s/n.trials
                                             if (input$show.coin) {
                                               layout(matrix(c(rep(1, 6), 0, 2, 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE))
                                               for (i in 1:input$flips) {
                                                 dev.hold()
                                                 plot(seq(0, input$flips), seq(0, 1, 1/input$flips), type = "n",
                                                      ylab = "Estimated P(Head)", xlab = "Trial")
                                                 abline(h = input$p.head, lty = 2, col = "gray")
                                                 lines(n.trials[1:i], cum.p[1:i], type = "l", col = 2)
                                                 plot(seq(0, 1), seq(0, 1), type = "n", xaxt = "n",
                                                      yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", bty = "n")
                                                 draw.circle(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, radius = 0.35, col = rgb(blue = 0.7,
                                                                                                        red = 0.7, green = 0.7, alpha = 0.8))
                                                 text(0.5, 0.5, ifelse(res[i] == 0, "TAIL", "HEAD"),
                                                      cex = 2.1)
                                                 dev.flush()
                                                 Sys.sleep(input$interval)
                                               }
                                             } else {
                                               for (i in 1:input$flips) {
                                                 plot(seq(0, input$flips), seq(0, 1, 1/input$flips), type = "n",
                                                      ylab = "Estimated P(Head)", xlab = "Trial")
                                                 abline(h = input$p.head, lty = 2, col = "gray")
                                                 lines(n.trials[1:i], cum.p[1:i], type = "l", col = 2)
                                               }
                                             }
})
})

Thank's!

messages.subject: Re: My loop not's working!
messages.body_plain:
So gentlemen!

I thought the bright shiny because I did not have any knowledge in html, java, or something. What I would like is that students could put values ​​for the parameters and tighten as a button "Go!" and immediately could see the entire simulation as stabilization of frequency as frequentist theory of probability. However, according to Alex, seems to be tedious to make this possible. Run it and see what I want people to view or students:

library(plotrix)
flips=1000
p.head=0.5
interval=0.001
res <- rbinom(n = flips, size = 1, prob = p.head)
n.trials <- seq(1, flips)

cum.s <- cumsum(res)
cum.p <- cum.s/n.trials

show.coin='yes'

layout(matrix(c(rep(1, 6), 0, 2, 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE))

for (i in 1:flips) {
  dev.hold()
  plot(seq(0, flips), seq(0, 1, 1/flips), type = "n",

       ylab = "Estimated P(Head)", xlab = "Trial")

  abline(h = p.head, lty = 2, col = "gray")

  lines(n.trials[1:i], cum.p[1:i], type = "l", col = 2)
  plot(seq(0, 1), seq(0, 1), type = "n", xaxt = "n",
       yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", bty = "n")
  draw.circle(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, radius = 0.35, col = rgb(blue = 0.7,
                                                         red = 0.7, green = 0.7, alpha = 0.8))
  text(0.5, 0.5, ifelse(res[i] == 0, "TAIL", "HEAD"),
       cex = 2.1)
  dev.flush()

  Sys.sleep(interval)
}

You can call Shiny.onInputChange(name, value) and that will act as if that control exists and was changed. However it can't be used while the page is loading; the Shiny client code must have fully initialized first.

This way we can directly let javascript manipulate the text input for which Shiny already has a binding defined. Note that you need to unbind all before letting javascript update a Shiny input variable and then bind them back again. This is required for reactivity to work. > > > > >                                              } else {
> > > > >                                                for (i in 1:input$flips) {

Hi, I didn't say it was tedious, just that the way you have proposed won't work.

Joe, assuming we have a computationally heavy workload that can be broken into slices, what's the best model to generate a reactivegraph at the end of it?

I was thinking you need to do the following tasks:

processing-step
reactive-graph upload
invalidate to cause loop back to reactive step.

the invalidation could be done by using a reactiveValue incremented at the end of each work step

x<-reactivePlot({
  somedata<-processingStep()
  reactiveValues$counter = reactiveValue$counter + 1
  plot(somedata)
}

I'm not sure quite whether the reactive will work like I hope here - since it's essentially invalidating itself.

What do you think?

-Alex
