messages.subject_clean: Pricing und conditions of Shiny Server hosting?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks a lot for getting back to me. If I had a couple of wishes, I'd wish for the following:

1) Secure access to shiny apps, i.e. only people with the right user credentials can see certain apps (ideally via OAuth 2.0)
2) HTTPS Requests to the shiny app and responses as JSON, so you can use the shiny app as a web service without the user interface - or is this already possible...?
3) Differentiated user permissions for each account with several users, i.e. one user has full admin rights, others can only access apps in their own folder - and these rights would be reflected in how RStudio functions as well. Or is this already possible...?

Thanks a lot and have a lovely weekend!

Ignacio

messages.body_plain:
Dear all, dear Shiny team,

I apologize if this is a trivial question or has been asked in this group before (I didn't see it mentioned though...) but I'd be very grateful for your answers:

Can I use a shiny app as a pure, secure REST web service? I only saw examples of HTML/shiny UIs but would it also be possible to make a shiny app simply a secure REST web service endpoint that...

* Takes and processes HTTP(S) requests?
* Returns the results of my R algorithms as JSON?
* Is secure in the sense that it is accessed via HTTPS and checks the user's credentials before running the algorithms?

I'd very grateful for any answers and pointers to example code.

Thanks so much in advance! Best,

Ignacio

messages.subject: Re: sizing shiny elements
messages.body_plain:
You have to change the relevant values to make things as big as you need them. See below

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that plots random distributions
shinyUI(

  pageWithSidebar(

    # Application title
    headerPanel("Clustering results"),

    # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
    sidebarPanel(
      tags$head(

        tags$style(type="text/css", "select { width: 400px; }"),

        tags$style(type="text/css", "textarea { max-width: 185px; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", ".jslider { max-width: 200px; }"),

        tags$style(type='text/css', ".well { max-width: 430px; }"),
        tags$style(type='text/css', ".span4 { max-width: 430px; }")

      ),

      helpText("There are 615 experiments\n",
               "and 230595 peptides.",
               "minExp = 2, minPep = 2."),

      selectInput("k","Method for choosing k for SVD:",
                  choices = c("Akaike information criteria (k = )", "Amended description length (k = )",
                              "Percentange of var. explained = 0.5 (k = )","Percentange of var. explained = 0.8 (k = )",
                              "Percentange of var. explained = 0.95 (k = )")
      )
    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Heatmap", plotOutput("heatmap",width = "800px", height = "800px")),

        #tabPanel("Heatmap", plotOutput("heatmap",width = "1000px", height = "900px")),
        tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary"))
      )
    )
  )
)

output$foo <- reactive({

})

messages.subject: Re: Don't show error messages
messages.body_plain:
Michal,

You can avoid these error messages being shown by modifying your script inside shinyServer.

For example, if you have a reactive output foo that is dependent on the value of an input element named bar, you can modify your code as shown below. The basic idea is to check if the input variable is set and execute the reactive function only if it is. This will avoid the errors you are talking about.

output$bar <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$foo)) {
    return()
  }
  ## rest of your code
})

messages.subject: download plot as pdf
messages.body_plain:
Dear Shiny-ers,

once more I return to you to figure out where I am going wrong in my attempts. I have a working script in shiny which generates some plots. The code runs on a 0.3.0 version of shiny, built on R 2.15.2 for 64-bit linux:

shiny /usr/lib64/R/library 0.3.0 NA R (>= 2.14.1) stats, tools, utils, datasets, methods, websockets (>= 1.1.6),
caTools, RJSONIO, xtable, digest NA markdown, Cairo, testthat NA NA GPL-3 2.15.2

I would, now, like to export those same plots to pdf, and offer my users the possibility of downloading them. After reading through the downloadButton/Link documentation, and the few threads in this forum, I've come up with the following setup.

>   # generates a path/string for the pdf filename
>   myFilename<-reactive(function(){sprintf("/var/tmp/Basename-%s.%s",input$jobName,'pdf')})
>   # the plot is generated in a (reactive) function called output$Plot
>   # the following lines, when inclued in the reactive function which generate the (lattice) plots, do work fine and produce a pdf in the expected folder.
>   # pdf(myFilename(), onefile=T, width=12,height=8)
>   # print(MySurfacePlot)
>   # dev.off()

This is how I tried to generate the pdf and connect it to the downloadHandler, within server.R

>   output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
>       filename = myFilename(),
>     # a function that actually opens a connection to a pdf and print the result to it
>     content = function(FILE=NULL) { # this function must take at least an input variable, namely the filename of the file to save
>    pdf(
>                    file=FILE, # hopefully this will catch the filename provided in the previous argument of the downloadHandler (filename=myFilename())
>                    onefile=T, width=12,height=8)
> print(output$Plot)
> dev.off()
> }
>   )

In the ui.R script, I insert the corresponding lines to tackle the downloadButton:

> downloadButton('download_P.C_Plot', label = "Download plot as PDF")

When I load the page, the program seems to run fine up to the point where I click on the downloadButton (or Link), which instead of initiating a download opens a new windows where the following error message is printed:

> invalid replacement for field ˜.label", should be from class "character" or a subclass (was class "NULL")

I googled the error code and it seems to refer to an issue which has been fixed already <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/91> - yet, I can't seem to get around it.

Is there something I didn't set correctly? Did I misunderstand the way the downloadHandler function works? Is the /var/tmp an issue for shiny (can it access outside its own app directory?)

Many thanks for any insights.

> Luca

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have also tried to provide a (simple) authentication to shiny-server applications. Therefore I installed the node.js module "http-auth" using npm (no, it did not work at the first attempt):
> npm install http-auth

As jphilip, I also manipulated "/usr/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/lib/proxy/http.js".
After the the first block of code where all the libraries are loaded I added:
> var auth = require('http-auth');
> var basic = auth({
>     authRealm : "Private area.",

messages.body_plain:
Dear Rstudio,

Sometimes I work with people who need someone to analyze private data.  I am intrigued by the idea of creating shiny applications that
can help them see and think about their own data.  I don't want my clients doing the model development, but I do want them to be able to change certain assumptions the model
makes about the data. I also want to provide them with the ability to do closed loop simulation studies of various choices.  Obviously, at present shiny is not capable of meeting my privacy
concerns.  However, in the future are you planning to be able to host shiny applications in secure environments?  In addition, if a user wanted to integrate Rcpp with shiny and run something
moderately computationally challenging (1core 100% for 5min) are you planning to be able to provide service?

Thank you for your help!!!

messages.subject: Re: download plot as pdf
messages.body_plain:
Hi Luca, a few things:

1) The first argument to downloadButton should be "downloadPlot". Also just in general, inputs and outputs must not have "." in their names as this confuses the web browser. (We really ought to have an error/warning...)

2) For downloadHandler(), the first argument should be "filename = myFilename" not "filename = myFilename()". You might also drop "reactive" from around the myFilename function, Shiny will call that function from a reactive context anyway. (Shouldn't matter much either way though.)

3) You can't print(output$Plot), outputs cannot be read in that way. And anyway, even if you could all you'd get is a base64-encoded PNG. You need to re-run the plotting operation inside of that content function (therefore it would be ideal if that plotting operation is in a function that can be accessed by both output$Plot and output$downloadPlot).

4) The myFilename function should only be returning a bare filename, without any directories; its job is to suggest to the browser what the user should save the file as.

5) Your comment "hopefully this will catch the filename..." doesn't reflect what actually happens--but it shouldn't matter. FILE is just the filename of a temp file that Shiny created, it shouldn't matter where it is or what the filename is. Just put your data in there and let Shiny take care of the rest.

Now all that said, there is ALSO the bug that you are currently hitting, which was fixed in GitHub but not released on CRAN yet (the CRAN folks requested that people not update packages more than every 1-2 months). In order to get the fix you will need to run this code:

install.packages("devtools") # if you don't have devtools already
devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server authentication?
messages.body_plain:
The entered username can be passed to the corresponding R instance by utilizing the AppSpec Object (appSpec instance) located in lib/worker/app-spec.js .
Inside the httpListener in lib/proxy/http.js (--> last post!) the following authentication code is inserted:

> basic.apply(req, res, function(username) {
>   router.getAppSpec_p(req, res)
>   .then(function(appSpec) {
>     appSpec.settings.loginName = username;
>   })
> });

This property of appSpec has to be passed to a newly spawned R process by altering lib/worker/app-worker.js around line 150. At the end of the parameter to "this.$proc.stdin.end", where the stdin ('command line') parameters of the R process are generated, the following line is added:
> (appSpec.settings.loginName || '') + '\n'
(Do not forget the additional "+" in the line above.)

Next the new command line parameter has to be added to the R environment. In "./R/SockJSAdapter.R" these parameters are read right at the beginning and are copied to the local R environment. Therefor the "Sys.setenv" function gets a new entry:
> USERNAME=input[4]
(Again do not forget to get the "," etc. right.)

Finally the provided username can be used inside the shiny (R) application:
> Sys.getenv('USERNAME')

 Yet again be aware that this is a crude hack by a highly inexperienced user (in fact I've seen any details about node.js for the first time about 24 ago :)

FloE

messages.subject: Re: download plot as pdf
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Jon,

With the suggested changes, the code correctly produces the pdf and sends it to the browser. Many thanks for helping me understand and fix this.
comments in line for the benefit pof others incurring similar problems:

On 20 February 2013 11:04, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> Hi Luca, a few things:
>
> 1) The first argument to downloadButton should be "downloadPlot". Also just in general, inputs and outputs must not have "." in their names as this confuses the web browser. (We really ought to have an error/warning...)

Ok, point 1 was a distraction from my side, when I simplified the code to post it here. I did anyway take out all '.' in variable names.

> 2) For downloadHandler(), the first argument should be "filename = myFilename" not "filename = myFilename()". You might also drop "reactive" from around the myFilename function, Shiny will call that function from a reactive context anyway. (Shouldn't matter much either way though.)

I've taken out that () - my first attempt was indeed to input just the function name but I was getting back an error.

>
> 3) You can't print(output$Plot), outputs cannot be read in that way. And anyway, even if you could all you'd get is a base64-encoded PNG. You need to re-run the plotting operation inside of that content function (therefore it would be ideal if that plotting operation is in a function that can be accessed by both output$Plot and output$downloadPlot).

OK, I created a function with all the plotting code, and which just return the plot upon call. This is then called by the reactivePlot and downloadPlot functions, like this:

# generates a path/string for the pdf filename

myPDF_PCfilename<-reactive(function(){sprintf("/var/tmp/Surface-PC-%s-%s.%s",input$UorE,input$jobName,'pdf')})

makePlot <- function() { #... code to make the plot...
  return(justGeneratedPlot)
}

output$PC_Plot <- reactivePlot(function() {
    print(make_PC_Plot())
})

output$download_PC_Plot <- downloadHandler(
      filename = myPDF_PCfilename,

    # a function that actually opens a connection to a pdf and print the result to it
    content = function(FILE=NULL) {

   pdf(file=FILE, onefile=T, width=12,height=8)
print(make_PC_Plot())
dev.off()
}
)

> 4) The myFilename function should only be returning a bare filename, without any directories; its job is to suggest to the browser what the user should save the file as.

Oh. I didn't get that from the manual - I somehow understood that it would be the location where the file is saved.

> 5) Your comment "hopefully this will catch the filename..." doesn't reflect what actually happens--but it shouldn't matter. FILE is just the filename of a temp file that Shiny created, it shouldn't matter where it is or what the filename is. Just put your data in there and let Shiny take care of the rest.

I will. I did.

>
> Now all that said, there is ALSO the bug that you are currently hitting, which was fixed in GitHub but not released on CRAN yet (the CRAN folks requested that people not update packages more than every 1-2 months). In order to get the fix you will need to run this code:
>
> install.packages("devtools") # if you don't have devtools already
> devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")

I'll pass this on to my sysadmin.

Again, thanks.

> Luca

> On Tue, Feb 19, 2013 at 5:42 AM, Luca Fenu <gufo...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear Shiny-ers,
> >
> > once more I return to you to figure out where I am going wrong in my attempts. I have a working script in shiny which generates some plots. The code runs on a 0.3.0 version of shiny, built on R 2.15.2 for 64-bit linux:
> >
> > shiny /usr/lib64/R/library 0.3.0 NA R (>= 2.14.1) stats, tools, utils, datasets, methods, websockets (>= 1.1.6),
> > caTools, RJSONIO, xtable, digest NA markdown, Cairo, testthat NA NA GPL-3 2.15.2
> >
> > I would, now, like to export those same plots to pdf, and offer my users the possibility of downloading them. After reading through the downloadButton/Link documentation, and the few threads in this forum, I've come up with the following setup.
> >
> > >   # generates a path/string for the pdf filename
> > >   myFilename<-reactive(function(){sprintf("/var/tmp/Basename-%s.%s",input$jobName,'pdf')})
> > >   # the plot is generated in a (reactive) function called output$Plot
> > >   # the following lines, when inclued in the reactive function which generate the (lattice) plots, do work fine and produce a pdf in the expected folder.
> > >   # pdf(myFilename(), onefile=T, width=12,height=8)
> > >   # print(MySurfacePlot)
> > >   # dev.off()
> >
> > This is how I tried to generate the pdf and connect it to the downloadHandler, within server.R
> >
> > >   output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
> > >       filename = myFilename(),
> > >     # a function that actually opens a connection to a pdf and print the result to it
> > >     content = function(FILE=NULL) { # this function must take at least an input variable, namely the filename of the file to save
> > >    pdf(
> > >                    file=FILE, # hopefully this will catch the filename provided in the previous argument of the downloadHandler (filename=myFilename())
> > >                    onefile=T, width=12,height=8)
> > > print(output$Plot)
> > > dev.off()
> > > }
> > >   )
> >
> > In the ui.R script, I insert the corresponding lines to tackle the downloadButton:
> >
> > > downloadButton('download_P.C_Plot', label = "Download plot as PDF")
> >
> > When I load the page, the program seems to run fine up to the point where I click on the downloadButton (or Link), which instead of initiating a download opens a new windows where the following error message is printed:
> >
> > > invalid replacement for field ˜.label", should be from class "character" or a subclass (was class "NULL")
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> >
> > I googled the error code and it seems to refer to an issue which has been fixed already <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/91> - yet, I can't seem to get around it.
> >
> > Is there something I didn't set correctly? Did I misunderstand the way the downloadHandler function works? Is the /var/tmp an issue for shiny (can it access outside its own app directory?)
> >
> > Many thanks for any insights.
> >
> > > Luca

The first part of your question would work fine locally, no problem; but for it to work from our server (glimmer.rstudio.com ), your SQL Server would need to be publicly accessible over the internet (which is generally just not a great practice security-wise). Or else, you would have to set up a scheduled task on one of your machines to dump your SQL Server data to a .csv file periodically and upload it to our servers. Then your Shiny app can do read.csv and use the head function to show just the top input$n rows. But regarding password protection, it is explicitly not supported on our servers right now nor by Shiny Server. There are a couple of options you have if running Linux (including cloud based like Amazon EC2), but if you only have access to Windows servers then we do not currently have an answer for you (but are hoping to later in the year). By the way, even if just running locally it is very very important that when you form the SQL query string you do it like this: vws <- sqlQuery(dbConnect, paste("SELECT TOP", as.numeric(input$n), "Datum, Sava, P1, P2, P3 FROM VWS ORDER BY ID DESC")) Without the "as.numeric" it would be easy for a malicious user to set input$n to "10 1; DROP TABLE VWS; --" for example, which would cause your whole database table to be erased! (This is called SQL injection and is probably the most common way websites get hacked.) messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server authentication?
messages.body_plain:
Simple authentication isn't an issue for me - they have to be authenticated in the local network to see the server anyway. I think the devs are looking to implement group-based LDAP authentication to allow for finer grained control over the various shiny applications.

On 21 February 2013 00:29, floe <flo...@endel.at> wrote:

> The entered username can be passed to the corresponding R instance by utilizing the AppSpec Object (appSpec instance) located in lib/worker/app-spec.js .
> Inside the httpListener in lib/proxy/http.js (--> last post!) the following authentication code is inserted:
>
> > basic.apply(req, res, function(username) {
> >   router.getAppSpec_p(req, res)
> >   .then(function(appSpec) {
> >     appSpec.settings.loginName = username;
> >   })
> > });
>
> This property of appSpec has to be passed to a newly spawned R process by altering lib/worker/app-worker.js around line 150. At the end of the parameter to "this.$proc.stdin.end", where the stdin ('command line') parameters of the R process are generated, the following line is added:
> > (appSpec.settings.loginName || '') + '\n'
> (Do not forget the additional "+" in the line above.)
>
> Next the new command line parameter has to be added to the R environment. In "./R/SockJSAdapter.R" these parameters are read right at the beginning and are copied to the local R environment. Therefor the "Sys.setenv" function gets a new entry:
> > USERNAME=input[4]
> (Again do not forget to get the "," etc. right.)
>
> Finally the provided username can be used inside the shiny (R) application:
> > Sys.getenv('USERNAME')
>
>  Yet again be aware that this is a crude hack by a highly inexperienced user (in fact I've seen any details about node.js for the first time about 24 ago :)
>
> FloE
>
>
> On Tuesday, February 19, 2013 8:01:24 PM UTC+1, floe wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I have also tried to provide a (simple) authentication to shiny-server applications. Therefore I installed the node.js module "http-auth" using npm (no, it did not work at the first attempt):
> > > npm install http-auth
> >
> > As jphilip, I also manipulated "/usr/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/lib/proxy/http.js".
> > After the the first block of code where all the libraries are loaded I added:
> > > var auth = require('http-auth');
> > > var basic = auth({
> > >     authRealm : "Private area.",
> > >     authList : ['user1:pwd1', 'user2:pwd2']
> > > });
> >
> > The authentication logic is applied directly to the httpListener. Therefore after
> > > this.httpListener = function(req, res) {
> > the following line is inserted:
> > > basic.apply(req, res, function(username) {});
> >
> > After saving and closing the file, the server has to be restarted.
> > Now when loading any site provided by shiny-server, username and password have to be entered.
> > Be aware that this is a very inflexible and unsafe hack.
> >
> > I would be most interesting how the entered username can be passed to the corresponding R instance(s)?!
> >
> > Hopefully a more intelligent authentication feature will be added to future versions :)
> >
> >
> > FloE
> >
> >
> > On Friday, January 18, 2013 9:51:43 PM UTC+1, jphilip wrote:
> > > Hello,
> > >
> > > I was able to add basic or digest authentication (only to the HTTP server) by just adding a reference to the http-auth node.js module as well as a few extra lines of code in the file http.js of the lib/proxy directory of the shiny-server package. (That goes for the power of node.js)
> > > I hard coded the user names and hashes in the file for now, but it seems it would be easy to have options in the config file for auth [None, Basic, Digest] and path to a paswd file.
> > >
> > > It does not seem to disrupt the application, but I did not do much testing. Also, I am not knowledgeable enough to know if authenticating the HTTP server is enough or if the potential websockets connection is a security hole.
> > >
> > > Would it be possible to add this type of basic/diggest auth to the open source version and leave LDAP and the likes for the enterprise version?
> > >
> > > Just a thought.
> > >
> > > Jacques
> > >
> > > On Wed, Jan 16, 2013 at 8:30 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > > This is planned for the "enterprise edition" of Shiny Server.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Wed, Jan 16, 2013 at 5:18 AM, Adam Edgley <adam....@gmail.com> wrote:

messages.subject: Re: problems with displaying href in table
messages.subject_clean: problems with displaying href in table
messages.body_plain:
I think the problem is that the xtable() function (which converts the object to an HTML table) won't write the raw HTML, which you are trying to do with the stuff. One way to do this is to write out the entire table yourself in html, and use htmlOutput() in the UI. Here's an example of generating a simple table. Note that this uses the shinyRun() function that I just posted a message about -- you should be able to simply copy and paste this code into your R session, and it will run the example: # Install downloader the first time install.packages('downloader') downloader::source_url("https://gist.github.com/wch/5003044/raw/aa4dbbca0023e29a629386b1ee9a5d27b2e37362/shinyserialize.r") shinyRun( #-------------------------------------------------------------- `server.R` = quote({ shinyServer(function(input, output) { output$test_table <- reactiveText(function() { str <- "\n" for (i in 1:input$n) { str <- paste(str, " \n", sep = "") for (j in 1:input$n) { str <- paste(str, " ", sep = "") } } str }) }) }), #-------------------------------------------------------------- `ui.R` = quote({ shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( headerPanel("HTML output"), sidebarPanel(sliderInput("n", "Number of on each side:", min = 0, max = 10, value = 5)), mainPanel(htmlOutput("test_table")) )) }) ) -Winston On Wed, Feb 20, 2013 at 11:23 AM, Ksenia Titorenko wrote: > yes, of course, I could > > ui.R: > > > > library(shiny) > > > > > > > > > # Define UI for application that plots random distributions > > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( > > > > > > # Application title > > > headerPanel("Results"), > > > sidebarPanel( > > > tags$head( > > > tags$style(type="text/css", "select { width: 400px; }"), > > > tags$style(type="text/css", "textarea { max-width: 185px; }"), > > > tags$style(type="text/css", ".jslider { max-width: 200px; }"), > > > tags$style(type='text/css', ".well { > numericInput("n", "Number of closest experiments to display:", 10) > > > ), > > > > > > > > > > > > # Show a plot of the generated distribution > > > mainPanel( > > > tableOutput("files") > > > ) > > > > > > )) > > server.R > > > library(shiny) > > > > > > shinyServer(function(input, output) { > > > > > > output$files <- reactiveTable(function() { > > > file<-paste(".//new_mzTab_files/PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_",input$files,".xml-mztab.txt",sep="") > > > ind<-which(human_files==file) > > > n=input$n > > > > > > messages.subject: Re: HTML Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Let's keep it friendly, everyone! :)

Rook is in the same category as the others. Can easily run out of a single R process (which you can do with Shiny as well, just call runApp() and leave your session alive) but it won't launch multiple R processes and manage them automatically. This is the job of Shiny Server, rApache, RServe, etc. and they all either don't work on Windows or won't launch multiple R processes on Windows. (At least that's my understanding, I don't have much experience with any of these packages except for Shiny.)

It's quite likely we will add Windows (and Mac) support to Shiny Server in the future, we expect there to be significant demand among Windows-only corporate users.

Ah, scoping bug. The "i" in the reactive function is late-bound. Try this (note the "local"):

for (x in 1:10) {local({
  i <- x

  output[[paste('result', i, sep='')]] <- reactive(function(){
    if (input[[paste('run', i, sep='')]] == 0)
      return()
    return(isolate({
      runCode(input[[paste('code', i, sep='')]])
    }))
  })

})}

messages.body_plain:
On Fri, Feb 22, 2013 at 11:11 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> Let's keep it friendly, everyone! :)
>
> Rook is in the same category as the others. Can easily run out of a single R
> process (which you can do with Shiny as well, just call runApp() and leave
> your session alive) but it won't launch multiple R processes and manage them
> automatically. This is the job of Shiny Server, rApache, RServe, etc. and
> they all either don't work on Windows or won't launch multiple R processes
> on Windows. (At least that's my understanding, I don't have much experience
> with any of these packages except for Shiny.)
>
> It's quite likely we will add Windows (and Mac) support to Shiny Server in
> the future, we expect there to be significant demand among Windows-only
> corporate users.

There are a few things that Windows doesn't do easily. Redis is a bear
to port to Windows because it takes advantage of a UNIX-ism that
allows a forked process to do copy on write, for example. But IIRC
Shiny Server uses Node.js for the "plumbing", and that does run on
Windows.

I've done a few tests with the Windows 8 Pro "Client Hyper-V" with
small Linux server guests. It's not quite as efficient as KVM or Linux
containers on the same laptop, but it's better than VMware Workstation
or VirtualBox. So if you must have a Linux server in a Windows
environment, Hyper-V is probably a viable option.

very enthusiastically I just upgraded to 0.4.0, and then file upload in my application didn't work any more. This is the relevant piece of code:

  values <- reactiveValues()

  output$loadData <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$upload)) {
        # User has not uploaded a file yet
        return(NULL)
      }

    fileInfo <- input$upload
    tmpDir <- tempfile()
    unzip(fileInfo$datapath, exdir=tmpDir)

    values$spectra <- getMqSpectra(tmpDir)
  })
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Anything known about this yet?

Otherwise: GREAT WORK!!! Previous to finding Shiny, I wrote GUIs for my software prototypes using Tk. But Shiny so much easier to write, and my users are absolutely excited about the look and feel w/ Shiny. Thx a lot for this package!

Regards
Christoph

Doug

messages.subject_clean: Rendering ggplots with a large underlying data.frame
messages.body_plain: Hi Doug - If you can pre-render your plots when the app starts, you might be able to come up with something that will work. But if you need to re-render the plots in response to user input, the single-threaded nature of R will cause blocking when the plots are re-rendered (although you might be able to speed things up with something like mclapply). So lets assume that you can pre-render all the plots at the beginning. This imposes the limitation that the plots have to be a predetermined size; they can't respond to changes in the browser window. I have a partial solution -- but you would need to figure out how to do the following: png('myfile.png') { ## Put some code here that will read an existing png file and output it } dev.off() ... because this renderPlot() wraps your block of code with the png() and dev.off() -- and, importantly, it decides the name of the file. As far as I know, there's no function that will do that. Another way to go is to make your own function based on renderPlot that can do this. At any rate, here's the skeleton code that I came up with (it needs that critical part filled in): downloader::source_url("https://gist.github.com/wch/5003044/raw/aa4dbbca0023e29a629386b1ee9a5d27b2e37362/shinyserialize.r") shinyRun( # -------------------------------------- `global.R` = quote({ min_bins <- 5 max_bins <- 20 }), # -------------------------------------- `ui.R` = quote({ shinyUI( pageWithSidebar( headerPanel(""), sidebarPanel( sliderInput("bins", "Bins", min=min_bins, max=max_bins, value=10) ), mainPanel( plotOutput("outplot") ) ) ) }), # -------------------------------------- `server.R` = quote({ library(ggplot2) library(png) shinyServer(function(input, output) { outfile_prefix <- tempfile() prerender <- function() { set.seed(456) dat <- data.frame(x=rnorm(400)) p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x)) for (bins in min_bins:max_bins) { filename <- paste(outfile_prefix, "-", bins, ".png", sep="") png(filename, width=400, height=400) print(p + geom_histogram(colour="black", fill="white", binwidth=diff(range(dat$x))/bins)) dev.off() } } # Render all the plots when the user connects to the session prerender() output$outplot <- renderPlot({ filename <- paste(outfile_prefix, "-", input$bins, ".png", sep="") ## Do something here that would read the saved file and write it out. ## It must work when this block of code is surrounded by png() and dev.off() }, width=400, height=400) }) }) ) Yet another option: If the images are rendered before the app even starts, then you could do something like this: * Store the images in www/ * use renderText() to generate raw HTML that contains an tag pointing to the selected image * display it with htmlOutput() You could even go further in this direction, and not use Shiny for this part -- you could do it with just Javascript. Ryan Mears had an example that did something like this. See this thread for more information: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/ITFUwvYE-f8/Pam8vqpxFQQJ -Winston On Mon, Feb 25, 2013 at 7:44 PM, Doug Mitarotonda wrote: > Hi, > I am not sure if this is better suited for the ggplot2 mailing list, but I will try here first since the use case is really tied to shiny. > > I am trying to plot a huge data.frame that takes up to 10 seconds to render. It becomes tiresome to have to wait 10 seconds every time I change an input parameter. Can I somehow pre-render all N images so that when the reactive input is resolved, all that needs to happen is a simple lookup instead of the full rendering of the ggplot? That way I can spend the computation time before launching the server (e.g., while I sleep) and the interface with shiny is very quick (e.g., when I interact with my boss). > > Many thanks, > Doug > -- > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "Shiny - Web Framework for R" group. > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to shiny-discus...@googlegroups.com. > For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/groups/opt_out. > >

> I have a question on how to keep running a Shiny server on the AWS.
> To start the server, I have to ssh to my AWS instance. So, after the server starts ("Starting listener"), it seems that I cannot quit the ssh session and consequently I have to leave the local machine used for this connection up.

the 'classical' way would be to use 'nohup' and '&'. I've never tried that together with 'sudo'. It would be something along the line of:

  nohup  sudo shiny-server &

The disadvantage would be that you completely use the connection to the process. An alternative would be to use 'screen' or, more modern, 'tmux': terminal multiplexers that allow you to reattach to a running process.

-Christoph

If you place your files in a directory called myapp/, you would run it with:
  runApp('myapp')

Or you could do:
  runApp('/path/to/myapp')

I would suggest that you not put them in the examples directory; not only is this meant just for examples, it will be removed and overwritten whenever you update the Shiny package to a new version.

-Winston

> Thank you for the instructions.

> Now, my question is that how I can stop my Shiny server after logging back into the shell.
> I searched on the internet looking for an answer but I have not found any so far. Most people talk about how to use the nohup before logging out from the shell but not about what to do after logging back.

;-) You will _not_ be able to reconnect to your shell to use C-c or something. This would work with screen or tmux.

When having used nohup, you'll have to search for your process in the process list:

  ps ax | grep shiny-server

, find the process ID and then kill it:

  kill ID

-Christoph

messages.body_plain:
First of all, regarding starting/stopping the shiny-server process, if you're using Ubuntu or CentOS 6 you can use the upstart script we provide, which will then automatically start shiny-server on startup and let you manually start/stop:

sudo wget\
  https://raw.github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/master/config/upstart/shiny-server.conf\
  -O /etc/init/shiny-server.conf

sudo start shiny-server

sudo stop shiny-server
As for installing sqldf, it's possible some prerequisites are missing, it would help to know what the console says when you attempt to install sqldf.

messages.body_plain: Hey Winston, Joe, Thanks for your feedback here. I took a look at bigvis and I am not sure that will help me as I have already summarized the data to be using stat = "identity". Winston, I will start working through your suggestions and see if I can get something working for me. Thanks for the help! Doug On Feb 25, 2013, at 9:40 PM, Winston Chang wrote: > Hi Doug - > > If you can pre-render your plots when the app starts, you might be able to come up with something that will work. But if you need to re-render the plots in response to user input, the single-threaded nature of R will cause blocking when the plots are re-rendered (although you might be able to speed things up with something like mclapply). > > So lets assume that you can pre-render all the plots at the beginning. This imposes the limitation that the plots have to be a predetermined size; they can't respond to changes in the browser window. > > I have a partial solution -- but you would need to figure out how to do the following: > png('myfile.png') > { > ## Put some code here that will read an existing png file and output it > } > dev.off() > > ... because this renderPlot() wraps your block of code with the png() and dev.off() -- and, importantly, it decides the name of the file. As far as I know, there's no function that will do that. Another way to go is to make your own function based on renderPlot that can do this. > > At any rate, here's the skeleton code that I came up with (it needs that critical part filled in): > > downloader::source_url("https://gist.github.com/wch/5003044/raw/aa4dbbca0023e29a629386b1ee9a5d27b2e37362/shinyserialize.r") > > shinyRun( > # -------------------------------------- > `global.R` = quote({ > min_bins <- 5 > max_bins <- 20 > }), > # -------------------------------------- > `ui.R` = quote({ > shinyUI( > pageWithSidebar( > headerPanel(""), > sidebarPanel( > sliderInput("bins", "Bins", min=min_bins, max=max_bins, value=10) > ), > mainPanel( > plotOutput("outplot") > ) > ) > ) > }), > # -------------------------------------- > `server.R` = quote({ > library(ggplot2) > library(png) > > shinyServer(function(input, output) { > outfile_prefix <- tempfile() > > prerender <- function() { > set.seed(456) > dat <- data.frame(x=rnorm(400)) > > p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x)) > > for (bins in min_bins:max_bins) { > filename <- paste(outfile_prefix, "-", bins, ".png", sep="") > png(filename, width=400, height=400) > print(p + geom_histogram(colour="black", fill="white", > binwidth=diff(range(dat$x))/bins)) > dev.off() > } > } > > # Render all the plots when the user connects to the session > prerender() > > output$outplot <- renderPlot({ > filename <- paste(outfile_prefix, "-", input$bins, ".png", sep="") > > ## Do something here that would read the saved file and write it out. > ## It must work when this block of code is surrounded by png() and dev.off() > > }, width=400, height=400) > }) > }) > ) > > > > Yet another option: If the images are rendered before the app even starts, then you could do something like this: > * Store the images in www/ > * use renderText() to generate raw HTML that contains an tag pointing to the selected image > * display it with htmlOutput() > > You could even go further in this direction, and not use Shiny for this part -- you could do it with just Javascript. Ryan Mears had an example that did something like this. See this thread for more information: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/ITFUwvYE-f8/Pam8vqpxFQQJ > > -Winston > > > On Mon, Feb 25, 2013 at 7:44 PM, Doug Mitarotonda wrote: > > Hi, > > I am not sure if this is better suited for the ggplot2 mailing list, but I will try here first since the use case is really tied to shiny. > > > > I am trying to plot a huge data.frame that takes up to 10 seconds to render. It becomes tiresome to have to wait 10 seconds every time I change an input parameter. My question: is there a way to "pre-render" the ggplots? > > > > For example, based on the inputs I have, there are N possible plots that could be created. Can I somehow pre-render all N images so that when the reactive input is resolved, all that needs to happen is a simple lookup instead of the full rendering of the ggplot? That way I can spend the computation time before launching the server (e.g., while I sleep) and the interface with shiny is very quick (e.g., when I interact with my boss). > > > > Many thanks, > > Doug > > > > -- > > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "Shiny - Web Framework for R" group. > > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to shiny-discus...@googlegroups.com. > > For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/groups/opt_out. > > > > > > > -- > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "Shiny - Web Framework for R" group. > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to shiny-discus...@googlegroups.com. > For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/groups/opt_out. > >

Hi everyone -

Just a quick notice about Glimmer: Due to a bug in the installed version of node.js, there was an issue on Glimmer where R sessions wouldn't get cleaned up after a connection was closed. You may have noticed a few hiccups in Glimmer's service today because of our work fixing the issue, but everything should be good now.

-Winston

I think you're right that being hidden is source of the issue. The hidden detection code is simple: if an object has zero width and zero height, then Shiny thinks it's hidden: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/www/shared/shiny.js#L1518 If you run options(shiny.trace=TRUE), you'll see this output with your app: RECV {"method":"init","data":{"dataset":"rock","obs:number":10,".shinyout_title_hidden":true,".shinyout_summary_hidden":false,".shinyout_view_hidden":false,"__allowDataUriScheme":true}} My guess is that what's happening is that the initial size of the object is 0x0 pixels, and so output$title is never run. You can force objects to not suspend by putting this in your shinyServer call: outputOptions(output, 'title', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE) But the appearance isn't quite right -- the nav bar overlaps the other stuff and looks like it doesn't really want to be that size. messages.body_plain:
In your call to shinyServer(), you can tell it to not suspend a particular object when hidden. For example, if your object is output$x, you'd do something like this:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$x <- renderText({ ... })

  outputOptions(output, 'x', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
})

messages.subject: renderPlot() error ... I think I'm missing something very simple
messages.subject_clean: renderPlot() error ... I think I'm missing something very simple
messages.body_plain:
Hi. I dove in with shiny late last year and a lot has changed since then. I am using the updated renderPlot() (rather than reactivePlot) function, but get the error:

> runApp()

Listening on port 8100
Error in serverFunc(input = .createReactiveValues(shinyapp$session, readonly = TRUE),  :
  could not find function "renderPlot"

I am porting some standalone code that generates plot using ggplot2. The code works (it produces the plot successfully) when I run it as I wrote it outside of this shiny setup, but I get the above error when I run it in the shiny framework. My code is below - the functions I use are stored in a global.R file, which loads when runApp() is called (I think). I can only figure that the 'renderPlot' is not not loaded in the workspace (i.e., the 'shiny' library is not loaded), but I load 'shiny' in each of the server.R and ui.R files.

tldr; I don't know why R can't find the 'renderPlot' function (???)

"server.R":

library(shiny)

library(ggplot2)

library(twitteR)

library(RColorBrewer)

# Define server logic required to plot variables against mpg

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # create a donut plot to be published to the shinyUI mainPanel()

  output$main_calorie_plot <- renderPlot({

    # run a funciton that collects tweets

    twitteR_df <- get_twitteR_df(input$Username)

    # turn the tweets into long-form data

    tweet_data <- get_tweet_data(twitteR_df)

    # subset the long-form tweet data

    range_data <- get_range_data(tweet_data, day = 0, span = 1)

    # process the range data into a form for get_main_calorie_plot(), which then uses ggplot2 to generate a donut plot

    graph_data <- get_graph_data(range_data, as.cals = F)

    # ... a function that uses ggplot2 to generate a donut plot

    donut_plot <- get_main_calorie_plot(range_data)

    ##### I believe this is how others are returning ggplot2 output, to be displayed in the shinyUI - ???

    print(donut_plot)

    #####

  })

})

"ui.R":

library(shiny)

# Define UI for Nutwition application

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Applicaiton title

  headerPanel('Nutwition'),

  sidebarPanel(

    # create a text input box, to collect the username

    textInput('Username', 'Username', 'nutwition_log'),

    # create a submit button that, when clicked, updates the mainPanel() plot

    submitButton('Update View')

  ),

  mainPanel(

    # I believe this is how ggplot2 plots are to be displayed in browser - ???

    plotOutput('main_calorie_plot')

  )

))

- Dan

PS I tried using reactivePlot() also (I read that this function has been deprecated), but received the following error:

> runApp()

Listening on port 8100

Error in tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers) :

  could not find function "func"

Killed

Every time I run the application and face this issue the port number changes.

Any help really appreciated.

messages.body_plain:
I have accidentally set-up a feedback cycle (using my URL sync logic), where a long latency reactive executes before the URL reactive.

This means that if the user updates an input faster than the long latency reactive operates, the hash update reverts the input to the prior state, and then to the new state, and then to the prior state (ad infinitum).

Can I specify that the URL updating output (just a reactive) should be sent to the client before the long latency one?

I vaguely recall a priority mechanism.

-Alex

messages.body_plain:
> Can I specify that the URL updating output (just a reactive) should be sent to the client before the long latency one?

It's not possible right now, and it's not immediately clear to me how we would do that. Currently we only send anything to the client when the server is at "equilibrium" (all reactive observers that wanted to execute have finished executing) because otherwise the outputs could be in an inconsistent state.

Would a simple fix be to disable all inputs while the server is calculating?

Perhaps another fix would be to have the input change ONLY trigger the URL logic on the server, which would then send an output to the client, which would only then update the server state that causes the long calculation to run. (You could use Shiny.onInputChange(name, value) for this latter one, at least for prototyping)

library(shiny)
library(datasets)

renderTimeSeries <- function(expr, env=parent.frame(), quoted=FALSE) {
  # Convert the expression + environment into a function
  func <- exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)

  function() {

    val <- func()
    list(start = tsp(val)[1],
         end = tsp(val)[2],
         freq = tsp(val)[3],
         data = as.vector(val))
  }
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    if (input$goButton == 0)
      return()

    # Take a dependency on input$goButton
    #input$goButton

    # Use isolate() to avoid dependency on input$obs
    dist <- isolate(rnorm(as.numeric(input$obs)))
    hist(dist)
  })

  output$timeSeries1 <- renderTimeSeries({

    ts(matrix(rnorm(300), 100, 3), start=c(1961, 1), frequency=12)
  })

})

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-server and x11
messages.body_plain:
As Winston mentioned, you shouldn't need X running to do base graphics, but if you are doing something fancier like RGL that does require XVFB, here's one way to do it:

http://trestletechnology.net/2013/02/graphical-tools-rgl-on-a-headless-shiny-server/

On Friday, February 8, 2013 4:46:32 AM UTC-6, Luca Fenu wrote:
> Hi, shiny-ers!
>
> We've managed to install and configure the shine-server to run on our linux server. My scripts run fine and the UI page is presented properly, but the graphics do not show - instead an error is reported:
>
> > ERROR: *X11 is not available.
>
> We tracked this down to the lack of a proper X-server on the machine, so we configured shiny-server to print  using a virtual
> framebuffer X (Xvfb). We modified the shiny-server startup script to run
> Xvfb and export DISPLAY=:3.1 - this worked fine for other softwares running on the machine.
> >
> > ws1 ~ # ps -ef | grep Xvfb
> > shiny     5205     1  0 15:10 ?        00:00:00 /usr/bin/Xvfb :3 -screen 1
> > 800x600x16
>
> Even when I explicitly defined the DISPLAY variable in the server.R like this:
> > Sys.setenv(DISPLAY = ":3.1")
> It didn't work and the error permains. In a last ditch attempt, I even tried to set
> > options(bitmapType="cairo")
> which I saw was a suggestion for a somewheat related problem in another thread.
>
> None of this fixes seems to work. Any idea on where I'm going wrong?
>
> Many thanks to whomever may point me in the right direction.
>
> > Luca
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

What is the best way to set the height argument of renderPlot based on the size of the data it's trying to plot?

Here is some pseudo code:

> getData = reactive({
> > #fetch data
> })
>
> plotFunc = function() {
> myData = getData()
> plot(myData)
> })
>
> plotHeight = reactive({
> myData = getData()
> if (length(myData) < 18)
> return(400)
> if (length(myData) >= 18)
> return(800)
> })
>
> output$plot  = renderPlot(plotFunc(),height=plotHeight,units="px")

This doesn't work as its nesting a reactive function plotHeight within another renderPlot.  I want to keep plotFunc as it's own function so that i can call upon it elsewhere.  I'm sure there is a simple answer, i'm just going code blind.

messages.subject: Re: Plot Rendering Differences
messages.body_plain:
It will depend on what platform the app is running on. Here are the default behaviors for different platforms:

* Mac: Points, lines, and text are antialiased.
* Linux: Points, lines, and text are antialiased, except for point shapes 16-18. (The default point shape for ggplot2 is 16.) Point centers are not aligned to the pixel grid, so they will have different, strange shapes.
* Windows: no antialiasing for points, lines, or text. Point centers will be aligned to the pixel grid, so they'll be consistent in shape.

It looks to me like your first image was created on Windows, and the second one was created on Linux. It also looks like you are using very thin vertical lines between the points -- on Windows, since there's no antialiasing, they'll be "expanded" to be one pixel wide, whereas on Linux (and Mac), lines that are thinner than one pixel will simply appear lighter, because of the antialiasing.

Fortunately, it is possible to get antialiasing on all objects. The CairoPNG() function from the Cairo package can be used for fully antialiased PNG output, and if you run install.packages('Cairo'), Shiny will automatically use it in renderPlot().

-Winston

messages.subject: Basics of Shiny 0.4.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have developed a simple app using the previous version of Shiny and it works fine.
A few days ago, I installed the newest version of Shiny and have tried to revise and run my app using it.
However, I have faced some problems with regard to the reactivity of the app.
When I first run the app, everything looks fine. I mean that the webpage displays the right outputs based on my defaults values. When I start changing my inputs, my main panel dose not get updated. I am aware of the changes in Shiny 0.4.0. However I am not able to resolve the problem.

For the sake of this post I have changed, renamed and shortened my app's elements.
What I am going to do using this app is to subset a master dataset and present some of the subset's characteristics.
So, I have an R function ("Fun_main") which takes care of subsetting using 5 inputs (MedicationName, CityName, StartDay, EndDay, and Dose). Any change to any of these 5 inputs should result in a different subset. Accordingly, the outputs "summary", "histogram", and "head" records change.

I have included below my server and ui codes revised based on my understanding from the Shiny 0.4.0.
Would you please help me find out why my app's reactivity feature does not work? In other words, my changes to the inputs do not change the outputs.

Thank you.

####Shiny UI####
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("My Test Application"),
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("MedicationName", "Choose a medication:", choices = c("aspirin", "amoxicillin", "acetaminophen", "cefazolin")),
    selectInput("CityName", "Choose a city", choices = c("miami", "buffalo")),
    selectInput("StartDay", "Start Day: ", choices = c("1", "2", "3")),
    selectInput("EndDay", "End Day: ", choices = c("15", "25", "35")),
    selectInput("Dose", "Dose: ", choices = c("10", "20", "30"))
  ),

  mainPanel(

    verbatimTextOutput("summary"),
    tableOutput("view"),
    plotOutput("main_plot")
  )
))

####Shiny Server####
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  source("Fun_main.R") #This is my R function which does subsetting

  MedicationNameInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$MedicationName,
           "aspirin" = aspirin,
           "amoxicillin" = amoxicillin,
           "acetaminophen" = acetaminophen,
           "cefazolin" = cefazolin)
  })

  CityNameInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$CityName,
           "miami" = miami,
           "buffalo" = buffalo)
  })

  StartDayInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$StartDay,
           "1" = 1,
           "2" = 2,
           "3" = 3)
  })

  EndDayInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$EndDay,
           "15" = 15,
           "25" = 25,
           "35" = 35)
  })

  DoseInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$Dose,
           "10" = 10,
           "20" = 20,
           "30" = 30)
  })

  subsetDataset <- reactive({

    Fun_main(input$MedicationName, input$CityName, input$StartDay, input$EndDay, input$Dose)

  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({

    subset <- subsetDataset()
    summary(subset)
  })

  output$view <- renderTable({

    subset <- subsetDataset()
    head(subset, n=5)
  })

  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    subset <- subsetDataset()
    Age <- unique(subset$AGE))
    hist(Age, probability = FALSE, breaks = 10, xlab = "Age Range (year)", main = "Subset's Age Distribution")
  })
})
